# @d3plus/core API Reference

| Charts                                        | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`Alluvial`](#alluvial)                       | Creates an alluvial (parallel sets) chart from plain data rows: one column per entry in `dimensions`, one node per category in each column, and bands between neighboring columns sized by how many rows (or how much `value`) flow between each pair of categories.                              |
| [`ArcDiagram`](#arcdiagram)                   | Places a network's nodes in a row along one line and draws each link as an arc between its two nodes, which shows the network's structure without a force layout's tangle, in an order you choose.                                                                                                |
| [`AreaPlot`](#areaplot)                       | Creates an area plot based on an array of data.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| [`BarChart`](#barchart)                       | Creates a bar chart based on an array of data.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| [`Beeswarm`](#beeswarm)                       | Creates a beeswarm from an array of data: each circle sits at its value along the axis set by `x` (or `y`), packed beside its neighbors so none overlap.                                                                                                                                          |
| [`BoxWhisker`](#boxwhisker)                   | Creates a simple box and whisker based on an array of data.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| [`BubbleChart`](#bubblechart)                 | Creates a bubble chart from an array of data: each row draws as a circle at its `x` and `y` values, sized by its `size` value.                                                                                                                                                                    |
| [`Bullet`](#bullet)                           | Creates a bullet graph from an array of data: one compact bar per row reading its `value` against qualitative `bands`, with a `target` marker, an optional `forecast` bar, and a value axis.                                                                                                      |
| [`BumpChart`](#bumpchart)                     | Creates a bump chart based on an array of data.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| [`Calendar`](#calendar)                       | Draws one square cell per day in a calendar grid, each colored by its `colorScale` value: weekdays down the side and weeks across, one block per year, with month outlines and localized weekday, month, and year labels.                                                                         |
| [`Candlestick`](#candlestick)                 | Creates a candlestick (or OHLC bar) chart of financial periods, from rows with a date and open, high, low, and close values.                                                                                                                                                                      |
| [`Chord`](#chord)                             | Creates a Chord diagram based on a defined set of nodes and links.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| [`Donut`](#donut)                             | Extends the Pie visualization to create a donut chart.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| [`Dumbbell`](#dumbbell)                       | Creates a dumbbell (range dot) chart from an array of data with one row per category and series, such as a country's value in 2010 and in 2020.                                                                                                                                                   |
| [`FanChart`](#fanchart)                       | Creates a fan chart from an array of data: a line per series with nested `confidence` bands around it, outermost first, shaded from the widest (lightest) to the narrowest (darkest).                                                                                                             |
| [`Funnel`](#funnel)                           | Creates a funnel chart from an array of data: one stage per row, in data order unless `sort` reorders them, drawn as a centered bar whose width encodes its value, with necks joining consecutive stages.                                                                                         |
| [`Gantt`](#gantt)                             | Creates a Gantt chart from an array of tasks: one labeled row per task, its bar running from `start` to `end` over a time axis.                                                                                                                                                                   |
| [`Gauge`](#gauge)                             | Creates a gauge (speedometer) from an array of data: a single dial that reads each row's `value` against its `domain`.                                                                                                                                                                            |
| [`Geomap`](#geomap)                           | Creates a geographical map with zooming, panning, image tiles, and the ability to layer choropleth paths and coordinate points.                                                                                                                                                                   |
| [`Hexbin`](#hexbin)                           | Creates a 2D binned density chart from raw observations: each row is a point at its `x` and `y` values (rows without numeric values are skipped), and the points are grouped into hexagons (`binShape`) of `binSize` pixels, colored on the colorScale by how many each holds (or by `binValue`). |
| [`Histogram`](#histogram)                     | Creates a histogram from an array of raw observations: the `value` of each row is binned along a linear x axis, and bar heights show each bin's count (or density / relative frequency via `binNormalize`, and running totals via `cumulative`).                                                  |
| [`Icicle`](#icicle)                           | Draws a hierarchy as nested rectangles, one band per `groupBy` level from the root edge out, where each node's breadth is proportional to its summed value.                                                                                                                                       |
| [`LinePlot`](#lineplot)                       | Creates a line plot based on an array of data.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| [`Lollipop`](#lollipop)                       | Creates a lollipop chart from an array of data: each row draws a thin stem from the baseline (or the value axis's break) to a circle at its value, with a category axis set by `discrete` (`"x"` draws vertical stems, `"y"` horizontal ones).                                                    |
| [`Marimekko`](#marimekko)                     | Creates a Marimekko (mosaic) chart from an array of data: one bar per discrete value (`x`), as wide as its `barWidth` (by default its total), with the bar's `groupBy` segments stacked to 100% of its height.                                                                                    |
| [`Matrix`](#matrix)                           | Creates a simple rows/columns Matrix view of any dataset.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| [`Network`](#network)                         | Creates a network visualization based on a defined set of nodes and edges.                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| [`Pack`](#pack)                               | Uses the d3 pack layout to create a Circle Packing chart based on an array of data.                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| [`ParallelCoordinates`](#parallelcoordinates) | Creates a parallel coordinates chart from an array of data: one axis per dimension and one line per row, crossing each axis at the row's value.                                                                                                                                                   |
| [`Pie`](#pie)                                 | Uses the d3 pie layout to create SVG arcs based on an array of data.                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| [`PolarArea`](#polararea)                     | Creates a polar area chart (Nightingale rose or coxcomb) from an array of data: every category gets an equal slice of the circle, and each wedge's radius shows its value.                                                                                                                        |
| [`Priestley`](#priestley)                     | Creates a Priestley timeline based on an array of data.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| [`Pyramid`](#pyramid)                         | Creates a population pyramid: horizontal bars for two groups (the first `groupBy` level, e.g. Male / Female) extending in opposite directions from a shared center line, one row per `y` category (e.g. age band).                                                                                |
| [`Radar`](#radar)                             | Creates a radar visualization based on an array of data.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| [`RadialBar`](#radialbar)                     | Creates a radial bar chart from an array of data: each row is a concentric track whose arc length shows its value, or, with `discrete("angle")`, a bar radiating out from an inner circle.                                                                                                        |
| [`RadialMatrix`](#radialmatrix)               | Creates a radial layout of a rows/columns Matrix of any dataset.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| [`Ridgeline`](#ridgeline)                     | Creates a ridgeline (joyplot) from an array of raw observations: the `value` of each row is summarized per group as a kernel density estimate, and each group's curve rises from its own baseline down the y axis, sharing the x axis.                                                            |
| [`Rings`](#rings)                             | Creates a ring visualization based on a defined set of nodes and edges.                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| [`Sankey`](#sankey)                           | Creates a Sankey visualization based on a defined set of nodes and links.                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| [`Scatter`](#scatter)                         | Creates a scatter plot from an array of data: each row draws as a point at its `x` and `y` values, on continuous axes (set `discrete` to place points along a category axis).                                                                                                                     |
| [`SlopeChart`](#slopechart)                   | Creates a slope chart from an array of data: a LinePlot comparing each series between two periods, with a line from its first value to its second.                                                                                                                                                |
| [`StackedArea`](#stackedarea)                 | Creates a stacked area plot based on an array of data.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| [`Streamgraph`](#streamgraph)                 | Creates a streamgraph from an array of data: a StackedArea whose layers flow around a central baseline instead of rising from zero.                                                                                                                                                               |
| [`Sunburst`](#sunburst)                       | Draws a hierarchy as concentric rings, one per `groupBy` level, where each node's arc angle is proportional to its summed value.                                                                                                                                                                  |
| [`Tree`](#tree)                               | Uses d3's tree layout to create a tidy tree chart based on an array of data.                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| [`Treemap`](#treemap)                         | Uses the d3 treemap layout to create SVG rectangles based on an array of data.                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| [`Violin`](#violin)                           | Creates a violin plot from an array of raw observations: the `value` of each row is summarized per group as a kernel density estimate, drawn as a mirrored curve around the group's category.                                                                                                     |
| [`Waffle`](#waffle)                           | Draws a grid of unit cells filled in order by category, each category getting cells in proportion to its value.                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| [`Waterfall`](#waterfall)                     | Creates a waterfall chart: one bar per category (`x`, or `y` with `discrete("y")` for horizontal bars) whose value is the change it makes to a running total.                                                                                                                                     |

| [`ConfidenceBandSetting`](#confidencebandsetting)   | One `confidence` band: a `[lower, upper]` pair, `[lower, upper, label]`, or a `{lower, upper, label}` object.                                                                                                                                                                      |
| [`ConfidenceBound`](#confidencebound)               | One `confidence` bound: a data key, an accessor, or `false` for none.                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| [`ConnectGaps`](#connectgaps)                       | Everything `connectGaps` takes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| [`ConstOrAccessor`](#constoraccessor)               | A value that can either be a function (called per-datum) or a literal that wraps as `constant(_)`.                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| [`CssColor`](#csscolor)                             | A CSS color string, like `"#4d79a7"`, `"rgb(77, 121, 167)"`, or `"transparent"`.                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| [`D3Selection`](#d3selection)                       | D3-style selection — deliberately loose.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| [`FacetConfig`](#facetconfig)                       | The object form of `facetConfig`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| [`FacetSort`](#facetsort)                           | Panel ordering: a named order, a comparator over facet values, or an explicit list of values.                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| [`FacetValue`](#facetvalue)                         | A value that splits the data into panels.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| [`FunnelConversion`](#funnelconversion)             | A conversion rate a stage's label can show.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| [`FunnelConversionOption`](#funnelconversionoption) | The `conversion` setting: one rate, both, or none.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| [`FunnelCurve`](#funnelcurve)                       | How the profile's width changes between two knots.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| [`GaugeIndicator`](#gaugeindicator)                 | How a gauge shows its value: a needle, or an arc filled from the minimum.                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| [`LinkOption`](#linkoption)                         | `link` as a group name, the full object form, or `false` for unlinked.                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| [`Orient`](#orient)                                 | Layout direction of a chart or Box shape.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| [`RangeBreakRule`](#rangebreakrule)                 | One stretch of time a time axis hides:                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| [`RangeBreakTime`](#rangebreaktime)                 | A time value a rule reads: a Date, a timestamp, or a date string.                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| [`SaveFormat`](#saveformat)                         | A file type the top-left download button can save the chart as.                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| [`SideOrient`](#sideorient)                         | Side a Whisker shape points toward.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| [`StringOrAccessor`](#stringoraccessor)             | A value that can be a function, a string key (wrapped in `accessor`), or a literal (wrapped in `constant`).                                                                                                                                                                        |

## Classes

<a id="area"></a>

### Area

Defined in: [shapes/Area.ts:25](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/shapes/Area.ts#L25)

Creates SVG areas based on an array of data.

#### Extends

- [`Shape`](#shape)

#### Config accessors

Each is a getter/setter: `.key(value)` sets it and returns the instance, `.key()` returns it. Also accepts the config accessors of [`Shape`](#shape).

| Accessor  | Type              | Default    | Description                                                                |
| --------- | ----------------- | ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `curve`   | `constoraccessor` | `function` |                                                                            |
| `defined` | `function`        | `function` | Determines whether a data point is defined (a gap in the area when false). |

<a id="classname"></a>

##### className()

###### Call Signature

> **className**(): `string` \| `string`[] \| `undefined`

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:250](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L250)

CSS classes added to the outermost element this chart or component draws
into, next to its fixed d3plus classes, so page CSS can target it: a
chart's root `<svg class="d3plus-viz">` (its `<canvas>` with the Canvas
renderer) and a standalone component's `<svg>`. Takes a space-separated
string or an array. A new value replaces the classes the previous one
added; unset adds none. Tooltips take their own `tooltipConfig.className`.

###### Returns

`string` \| `string`[] \| `undefined`

###### Example

```ts
new d3plus.BarChart().className("revenue-chart dark");
```

###### Inherited from

[`Shape`](#shape).[`className`](#classname-16)

string or an array. A new value replaces the classes the previous one
added; unset adds none. Tooltips take their own `tooltipConfig.className`.

<a id="colordefaults"></a>

##### colorDefaults()

###### Call Signature

> **colorDefaults**(): `ColorDefaults`

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:283](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L283)

Overrides the default colors used when assigning fills from data and choosing legible text colors: `dark` and `light` (the text colors picked for contrast against a background), `missing` (null/undefined values), `on`/`off` (`true`/`false` values), `sequential` (the anchor hue for magnitude ramps), and `scale` (the categorical palette, given as a d3 ordinal scale or an array of colors). Keys are merged into the current defaults, and a Viz passes its overrides down to the shapes and components it draws.

###### Returns

`ColorDefaults`

###### Example

```ts
new Treemap().colorDefaults({
  dark: "#222",
  light: "#fff",
  scale: ["#1b9e77", "#d95f02", "#7570b3"],
});
```

> **locale**(): `string`

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:231](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L231)

The locale used for all text and number formatting. Supports the locales defined in [d3plus-format](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus-format/blob/master/src/locale.js). The locale can be a complex Object, a locale code (like "en-US"), or a 2-digit language code (like "en"). If a 2-digit code is provided, the "findLocale" function is used to identify the most approximate locale.

###### Returns

`string`

###### Example

```ts
{
        separator: "",
        suffixes: ["y", "z", "a", "f", "p", "n", "\u00b5", "m", "", "k", "M", "B", "t", "q", "Q", "Z", "Y"],
        grouping: [3],
        delimiters: {
          thousands: ",",
          decimal: "."
        },
        currency: ["$", ""]
      }
```

Event listener for the specified event _typenames_. Mirrors the core [d3-selection](https://github.com/d3/d3-selection#selection_on) behavior.

###### Returns

`Record`\<`string`, (...`args`: `unknown`[]) => `unknown`\>

**By default, listeners apply globally to all objects, however, passing a namespace with the class name gives control over specific elements:**

```ts
new Plot.on("click.Shape", function (d) {
  console.log("data for shape clicked:", d);
}).on("click.Legend", function (d) {
  console.log("data for legend clicked:", d);
});
```

<a id="translate"></a>

##### translate()

###### Call Signature

> **translate**(): (`d`: `string`, `locale?`: `string`) => `string`

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:347](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L347)

Defines how informational text strings should be displayed. By default, this function will try to find the string in question (which is the first argument provided to this function) inside of an internally managed translation Object. If you'd like to override to use custom text, simply pass this method your own custom formatting function.

###### Returns

(`d`: `string`, `locale?`: `string`) => `string`

###### Example

**For example, if we wanted to only change the string "Back" and allow all other string to return in English:**

```ts
.translate(function(d) {
return d === "Back" ? "Get outta here" : d;
})
```

Overrides the default colors used when assigning fills from data and choosing legible text colors: `dark` and `light` (the text colors picked for contrast against a background), `missing` (null/undefined values), `on`/`off` (`true`/`false` values), `sequential` (the anchor hue for magnitude ramps), and `scale` (the categorical palette, given as a d3 ordinal scale or an array of colors). Keys are merged into the current defaults, and a Viz passes its overrides down to the shapes and components it draws.

###### Example

```ts
new Treemap().colorDefaults({
  dark: "#222",
  light: "#fff",
  scale: ["#1b9e77", "#d95f02", "#7570b3"],
});
```

Keys are merged into the current defaults, and a Viz passes its overrides down to the shapes and components it draws.

| `_`       | [`ColorDefaultsConfig`](#colordefaultsconfig) |

`this`

###### Example

```ts
new Treemap().colorDefaults({
  dark: "#222",
  light: "#fff",
  scale: ["#1b9e77", "#d95f02", "#7570b3"],
});
```

<a id="labelrotation"></a>

##### labelRotation()

###### Call Signature

> **labelRotation**(): `number` \| `boolean` \| `undefined`

Defined in: [components/Axis/Axis.ts:517](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/components/Axis/Axis.ts#L517)

Whether to rotate the axis labels, and by how much. `true` rotates
them -90 degrees and `false` keeps them flat. Left `undefined` (the
default), a horizontal axis of categories rotates its labels when any
label would not fit its share of the axis whole (a word dropped, cut
off, or broken across lines) or would overlap its neighbor: they
slant 30 degrees (-30 on a bottom axis, 30 on a top one), or stand at
-90 when even slanted they would leave more labels cut short or
hidden. A vertical axis never rotates its labels on its own. A number
rotates them by that many degrees (clockwise, so `-45` rises to the
right): each label hangs off the axis from the end of its text
nearest the axis, which sits across from its tick, so on a bottom
axis a negative angle ends each label at its tick and a positive one
starts it there. Angles outside -90 to 90 turn a half turn to read
left to right (`135` draws as `-45`), and `0` keeps the labels flat.
Slanted labels wrap between words onto up to three lines, as many as
fit between neighboring labels, so they reach less far from the
axis. Labels that still overlap once rotated are thinned evenly.

###### Returns

`number` \| `boolean` \| `undefined`

###### Call Signature

> **labelRotation**(`_`: `number` \| `boolean` \| `undefined`): `this`

##### locale()

> **locale**(): `string`

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:231](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L231)

The locale used for all text and number formatting. Supports the locales defined in [d3plus-format](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus-format/blob/master/src/locale.js). The locale can be a complex Object, a locale code (like "en-US"), or a 2-digit language code (like "en"). If a 2-digit code is provided, the "findLocale" function is used to identify the most approximate locale.

###### Returns

`string`

###### Example

```ts
{
        separator: "",
        suffixes: ["y", "z", "a", "f", "p", "n", "\u00b5", "m", "", "k", "M", "B", "t", "q", "Q", "Z", "Y"],
        grouping: [3],
        delimiters: {
          thousands: ",",
          decimal: "."
        },
        currency: ["$", ""]
      }
```

<a id="measure"></a>

##### measure()

> **measure**(): `this`

Defined in: [components/Axis/Axis.ts:573](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/components/Axis/Axis.ts#L573)

Runs the layout pass only — scale construction, tick selection, label
textWrap, and outerBounds — with **no DOM access**. After it returns,
`outerBounds()` / `_d3Scale` / `_getPosition()` are populated exactly as
they would be after a full `render()`, but no `<svg>`, `<g>`, tick shapes,
or label TextBoxes are created. Answers "how much room will this axis
need?" without rendering; Plot uses it to size its test-axes. Delegates to
the standalone `measureAxis(axis)` in axisLayout.ts, so callers can run
layout without owning an Axis instance.

###### Returns

`this`

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:347](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L347)

Defines how informational text strings should be displayed. By default, this function will try to find the string in question (which is the first argument provided to this function) inside of an internally managed translation Object. If you'd like to override to use custom text, simply pass this method your own custom formatting function.

###### Returns

(`d`: `string`, `locale?`: `string`) => `string`

###### Example

**For example, if we wanted to only change the string "Back" and allow all other string to return in English:**

```ts
.translate(function(d) {
return d === "Back" ? "Get outta here" : d;
})
```

<a id="labelrotation-1"></a>

##### labelRotation()

###### Call Signature

> **labelRotation**(): `number` \| `boolean` \| `undefined`

Defined in: [components/Axis/Axis.ts:517](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/components/Axis/Axis.ts#L517)

Whether to rotate the axis labels, and by how much. `true` rotates
them -90 degrees and `false` keeps them flat. Left `undefined` (the
default), a horizontal axis of categories rotates its labels when any
label would not fit its share of the axis whole (a word dropped, cut
off, or broken across lines) or would overlap its neighbor: they
slant 30 degrees (-30 on a bottom axis, 30 on a top one), or stand at
-90 when even slanted they would leave more labels cut short or
hidden. A vertical axis never rotates its labels on its own. A number
rotates them by that many degrees (clockwise, so `-45` rises to the
right): each label hangs off the axis from the end of its text
nearest the axis, which sits across from its tick, so on a bottom
axis a negative angle ends each label at its tick and a positive one
starts it there. Angles outside -90 to 90 turn a half turn to read
left to right (`135` draws as `-45`), and `0` keeps the labels flat.
Slanted labels wrap between words onto up to three lines, as many as
fit between neighboring labels, so they reach less far from the
axis. Labels that still overlap once rotated are thinned evenly.

###### Returns

`number` \| `boolean` \| `undefined`

###### Inherited from

[`Axis`](#axis).[`labelRotation`](#labelrotation)

> **locale**(): `string`

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:231](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L231)

The locale used for all text and number formatting. Supports the locales defined in [d3plus-format](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus-format/blob/master/src/locale.js). The locale can be a complex Object, a locale code (like "en-US"), or a 2-digit language code (like "en"). If a 2-digit code is provided, the "findLocale" function is used to identify the most approximate locale.

```ts
        separator: "",
        suffixes: ["y", "z", "a", "f", "p", "n", "\u00b5", "m", "", "k", "M", "B", "t", "q", "Q", "Z", "Y"],
        grouping: [3],
        delimiters: {
          thousands: ",",
          decimal: "."
        },
        currency: ["$", ""]
      }
```

<a id="measure-1"></a>

##### measure()

> **measure**(): `this`

Defined in: [components/Axis/Axis.ts:573](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/components/Axis/Axis.ts#L573)

Runs the layout pass only — scale construction, tick selection, label
textWrap, and outerBounds — with **no DOM access**. After it returns,
`outerBounds()` / `_d3Scale` / `_getPosition()` are populated exactly as
they would be after a full `render()`, but no `<svg>`, `<g>`, tick shapes,
or label TextBoxes are created. Answers "how much room will this axis
need?" without rendering; Plot uses it to size its test-axes. Delegates to
the standalone `measureAxis(axis)` in axisLayout.ts, so callers can run
layout without owning an Axis instance.

###### Returns

`this`

##### translate()

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:347](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L347)

Defines how informational text strings should be displayed. By default, this function will try to find the string in question (which is the first argument provided to this function) inside of an internally managed translation Object. If you'd like to override to use custom text, simply pass this method your own custom formatting function.

###### Returns

(`d`: `string`, `locale?`: `string`) => `string`

###### Example

**For example, if we wanted to only change the string "Back" and allow all other string to return in English:**

```ts
.translate(function(d) {
return d === "Back" ? "Get outta here" : d;
})
```

Overrides the default colors used when assigning fills from data and choosing legible text colors: `dark` and `light` (the text colors picked for contrast against a background), `missing` (null/undefined values), `on`/`off` (`true`/`false` values), `sequential` (the anchor hue for magnitude ramps), and `scale` (the categorical palette, given as a d3 ordinal scale or an array of colors). <a id="labelrotation-2"></a>

##### labelRotation()

###### Call Signature

> **labelRotation**(): `number` \| `boolean` \| `undefined`

Defined in: [components/Axis/Axis.ts:517](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/components/Axis/Axis.ts#L517)

Whether to rotate the axis labels, and by how much. `true` rotates
them -90 degrees and `false` keeps them flat. Left `undefined` (the
default), a horizontal axis of categories rotates its labels when any
label would not fit its share of the axis whole (a word dropped, cut
off, or broken across lines) or would overlap its neighbor: they
slant 30 degrees (-30 on a bottom axis, 30 on a top one), or stand at
-90 when even slanted they would leave more labels cut short or
hidden. A vertical axis never rotates its labels on its own. A number
rotates them by that many degrees (clockwise, so `-45` rises to the
right): each label hangs off the axis from the end of its text
nearest the axis, which sits across from its tick, so on a bottom
axis a negative angle ends each label at its tick and a positive one
starts it there. Angles outside -90 to 90 turn a half turn to read
left to right (`135` draws as `-45`), and `0` keeps the labels flat.
Slanted labels wrap between words onto up to three lines, as many as
fit between neighboring labels, so they reach less far from the
axis. Labels that still overlap once rotated are thinned evenly.

###### Returns

`number` \| `boolean` \| `undefined`

###### Inherited from

[`Axis`](#axis).[`labelRotation`](#labelrotation)

The locale used for all text and number formatting. Supports the locales defined in [d3plus-format](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus-format/blob/master/src/locale.js). The locale can be a complex Object, a locale code (like "en-US"), or a 2-digit language code (like "en").         grouping: [3],
```ts
        delimiters: {
```

<a id="measure-2"></a>

##### measure()

> **measure**(): `this`

Defined in: [components/Axis/Axis.ts:573](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/components/Axis/Axis.ts#L573)

Runs the layout pass only — scale construction, tick selection, label
textWrap, and outerBounds — with **no DOM access**. After it returns,
`outerBounds()` / `_d3Scale` / `_getPosition()` are populated exactly as
they would be after a full `render()`, but no `<svg>`, `<g>`, tick shapes,
or label TextBoxes are created. Answers "how much room will this axis
need?" without rendering; Plot uses it to size its test-axes. Delegates to
the standalone `measureAxis(axis)` in axisLayout.ts, so callers can run
layout without owning an Axis instance.

###### Returns

`this`

`this`

###### Example

**By default, listeners apply globally to all objects, however, passing a namespace with the class name gives control over specific elements:**

```ts
new Plot.on("click.Shape", function (d) {
  console.log("data for shape clicked:", d);
}).on("click.Legend", function (d) {

});
```

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:347](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L347)

Defines how informational text strings should be displayed. By default, this function will try to find the string in question (which is the first argument provided to this function) inside of an internally managed translation Object. If you'd like to override to use custom text, simply pass this method your own custom formatting function.

###### Returns

(`d`: `string`, `locale?`: `string`) => `string`

###### Example

**For example, if we wanted to only change the string "Back" and allow all other string to return in English:**

```ts
.translate(function(d) {
return d === "Back" ? "Get outta here" : d;
})
```

Overrides the default colors used when assigning fills from data and choosing legible text colors: `dark` and `light` (the text colors picked for contrast against a background), `missing` (null/undefined values), `on`/`off` (`true`/`false` values), `sequential` (the anchor hue for magnitude ramps), and `scale` (the categorical palette, given as a d3 ordinal scale or an array of colors). <a id="labelrotation-3"></a>

##### labelRotation()

###### Call Signature

> **labelRotation**(): `number` \| `boolean` \| `undefined`

Defined in: [components/Axis/Axis.ts:517](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/components/Axis/Axis.ts#L517)

Whether to rotate the axis labels, and by how much. `true` rotates
them -90 degrees and `false` keeps them flat. Left `undefined` (the
default), a horizontal axis of categories rotates its labels when any
label would not fit its share of the axis whole (a word dropped, cut
off, or broken across lines) or would overlap its neighbor: they
slant 30 degrees (-30 on a bottom axis, 30 on a top one), or stand at
-90 when even slanted they would leave more labels cut short or
hidden. A vertical axis never rotates its labels on its own. A number
rotates them by that many degrees (clockwise, so `-45` rises to the
right): each label hangs off the axis from the end of its text
nearest the axis, which sits across from its tick, so on a bottom
axis a negative angle ends each label at its tick and a positive one
starts it there. Angles outside -90 to 90 turn a half turn to read
left to right (`135` draws as `-45`), and `0` keeps the labels flat.
Slanted labels wrap between words onto up to three lines, as many as
fit between neighboring labels, so they reach less far from the
axis. Labels that still overlap once rotated are thinned evenly.

###### Returns

`number` \| `boolean` \| `undefined`

###### Inherited from

[`Axis`](#axis).[`labelRotation`](#labelrotation)

> **labelRotation**(`_`: `number` \| `boolean` \| `undefined`): `this`

left to right (`135` draws as `-45`), and `0` keeps the labels flat.
Slanted labels wrap between words onto up to three lines, as many as
fit between neighboring labels, so they reach less far from the
axis. Labels that still overlap once rotated are thinned evenly.

<a id="measure-3"></a>

##### measure()

> **measure**(): `this`

Defined in: [components/Axis/Axis.ts:573](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/components/Axis/Axis.ts#L573)

Runs the layout pass only — scale construction, tick selection, label
textWrap, and outerBounds — with **no DOM access**. After it returns,
`outerBounds()` / `_d3Scale` / `_getPosition()` are populated exactly as
they would be after a full `render()`, but no `<svg>`, `<g>`, tick shapes,
or label TextBoxes are created. Answers "how much room will this axis
need?" without rendering; Plot uses it to size its test-axes. Delegates to
the standalone `measureAxis(axis)` in axisLayout.ts, so callers can run
layout without owning an Axis instance.

###### Returns

`this`

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:347](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L347)

Defines how informational text strings should be displayed. By default, this function will try to find the string in question (which is the first argument provided to this function) inside of an internally managed translation Object. If you'd like to override to use custom text, simply pass this method your own custom formatting function.

###### Returns

(`d`: `string`, `locale?`: `string`) => `string`

###### Example

**For example, if we wanted to only change the string "Back" and allow all other string to return in English:**

```ts
.translate(function(d) {
return d === "Back" ? "Get outta here" : d;
})
```

Overrides the default colors used when assigning fills from data and choosing legible text colors: `dark` and `light` (the text colors picked for contrast against a background), `missing` (null/undefined values), `on`/`off` (`true`/`false` values), `sequential` (the anchor hue for magnitude ramps), and `scale` (the categorical palette, given as a d3 ordinal scale or an array of colors). Keys are merged into the current defaults, and a Viz passes its overrides down to the shapes and components it draws.

```ts
  light: "#fff",
  scale: ["#1b9e77", "#d95f02", "#7570b3"],
});
```

<a id="labelrotation-4"></a>

##### labelRotation()

###### Call Signature

> **labelRotation**(): `number` \| `boolean` \| `undefined`

Defined in: [components/Axis/Axis.ts:517](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/components/Axis/Axis.ts#L517)

Whether to rotate the axis labels, and by how much. `true` rotates
them -90 degrees and `false` keeps them flat. Left `undefined` (the
default), a horizontal axis of categories rotates its labels when any
label would not fit its share of the axis whole (a word dropped, cut
off, or broken across lines) or would overlap its neighbor: they
slant 30 degrees (-30 on a bottom axis, 30 on a top one), or stand at
-90 when even slanted they would leave more labels cut short or
hidden. A vertical axis never rotates its labels on its own. A number
rotates them by that many degrees (clockwise, so `-45` rises to the
right): each label hangs off the axis from the end of its text
nearest the axis, which sits across from its tick, so on a bottom
axis a negative angle ends each label at its tick and a positive one
starts it there. Angles outside -90 to 90 turn a half turn to read
left to right (`135` draws as `-45`), and `0` keeps the labels flat.
Slanted labels wrap between words onto up to three lines, as many as
fit between neighboring labels, so they reach less far from the
axis. Labels that still overlap once rotated are thinned evenly.

###### Returns

`number` \| `boolean` \| `undefined`

###### Inherited from

[`Axis`](#axis).[`labelRotation`](#labelrotation)

The locale used for all text and number formatting. Supports the locales defined in [d3plus-format](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus-format/blob/master/src/locale.js). The locale can be a complex Object, a locale code (like "en-US"), or a 2-digit language code (like "en").         grouping: [3],

```ts
          decimal: "."

        currency: ["$", ""]
      }
```

<a id="measure-4"></a>

##### measure()

> **measure**(): `this`

Defined in: [components/Axis/Axis.ts:573](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/components/Axis/Axis.ts#L573)

Runs the layout pass only — scale construction, tick selection, label
textWrap, and outerBounds — with **no DOM access**. After it returns,
`outerBounds()` / `_d3Scale` / `_getPosition()` are populated exactly as
they would be after a full `render()`, but no `<svg>`, `<g>`, tick shapes,
or label TextBoxes are created. Answers "how much room will this axis
need?" without rendering; Plot uses it to size its test-axes. Delegates to
the standalone `measureAxis(axis)` in axisLayout.ts, so callers can run
layout without owning an Axis instance.

###### Returns

`this`

Defines how informational text strings should be displayed. CSS classes added to the outermost element this chart or component draws
into, next to its fixed d3plus classes, so page CSS can target it: a
chart's root `<svg class="d3plus-viz">` (its `<canvas>` with the Canvas
renderer) and a standalone component's `<svg>`. Takes a space-separated
string or an array. A new value replaces the classes the previous one
added; unset adds none. Tooltips take their own `tooltipConfig.className`.

<a id="colordefaults-6"></a>

##### colorDefaults()

###### Call Signature

> **colorDefaults**(): `ColorDefaults`

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:283](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L283)

Overrides the default colors used when assigning fills from data and choosing legible text colors: `dark` and `light` (the text colors picked for contrast against a background), `missing` (null/undefined values), `on`/`off` (`true`/`false` values), `sequential` (the anchor hue for magnitude ramps), and `scale` (the categorical palette, given as a d3 ordinal scale or an array of colors). Keys are merged into the current defaults, and a Viz passes its overrides down to the shapes and components it draws.

###### Returns

`ColorDefaults`

###### Example

```ts
new Treemap().colorDefaults({
  dark: "#222",
  light: "#fff",
  scale: ["#1b9e77", "#d95f02", "#7570b3"],
});
```

> **locale**(): `string`

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:231](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L231)

The locale used for all text and number formatting. Supports the locales defined in [d3plus-format](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus-format/blob/master/src/locale.js). The locale can be a complex Object, a locale code (like "en-US"), or a 2-digit language code (like "en"). If a 2-digit code is provided, the "findLocale" function is used to identify the most approximate locale.

###### Returns

`string`

###### Example

```ts
{
        separator: "",
        suffixes: ["y", "z", "a", "f", "p", "n", "\u00b5", "m", "", "k", "M", "B", "t", "q", "Q", "Z", "Y"],
        grouping: [3],
        delimiters: {
          thousands: ",",
          decimal: "."
        },
        currency: ["$", ""]
      }
```

Event listener for the specified event _typenames_. Mirrors the core [d3-selection](https://github.com/d3/d3-selection#selection_on) behavior.

```ts
});
```

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:347](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L347)

Defines how informational text strings should be displayed. By default, this function will try to find the string in question (which is the first argument provided to this function) inside of an internally managed translation Object. If you'd like to override to use custom text, simply pass this method your own custom formatting function.

###### Returns

(`d`: `string`, `locale?`: `string`) => `string`

###### Example

**For example, if we wanted to only change the string "Back" and allow all other string to return in English:**

```ts
.translate(function(d) {
return d === "Back" ? "Get outta here" : d;
})
```

CSS classes added to the outermost element this chart or component draws
into, next to its fixed d3plus classes, so page CSS can target it: a
chart's root `<svg class="d3plus-viz">` (its `<canvas>` with the Canvas
renderer) and a standalone component's `<svg>`. Takes a space-separated
string or an array. A new value replaces the classes the previous one
added; unset adds none. Tooltips take their own `tooltipConfig.className`.

```ts
new d3plus.BarChart().className("revenue-chart dark");
```

<a id="colordefaults-7"></a>

##### colorDefaults()

###### Call Signature

> **colorDefaults**(): `ColorDefaults`

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:283](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L283)

Overrides the default colors used when assigning fills from data and choosing legible text colors: `dark` and `light` (the text colors picked for contrast against a background), `missing` (null/undefined values), `on`/`off` (`true`/`false` values), `sequential` (the anchor hue for magnitude ramps), and `scale` (the categorical palette, given as a d3 ordinal scale or an array of colors). Keys are merged into the current defaults, and a Viz passes its overrides down to the shapes and components it draws.

###### Returns

`ColorDefaults`

###### Example

```ts
new Treemap().colorDefaults({
  dark: "#222",
  light: "#fff",
  scale: ["#1b9e77", "#d95f02", "#7570b3"],
});
```

<a id="locale-7"></a>

##### locale()

###### Call Signature

> **locale**(): `string`

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:231](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L231)

The locale used for all text and number formatting. Supports the locales defined in [d3plus-format](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus-format/blob/master/src/locale.js). The locale can be a complex Object, a locale code (like "en-US"), or a 2-digit language code (like "en"). If a 2-digit code is provided, the "findLocale" function is used to identify the most approximate locale.

###### Returns

`string`

###### Example

```ts
{
        separator: "",
        suffixes: ["y", "z", "a", "f", "p", "n", "\u00b5", "m", "", "k", "M", "B", "t", "q", "Q", "Z", "Y"],
        grouping: [3],
        delimiters: {
          thousands: ",",
          decimal: "."
        },
        currency: ["$", ""]
      }
```

<a id="on-7"></a>

##### on()

###### Call Signature

> **on**(): `Record`\<`string`, (...`args`: `unknown`[]) => `unknown`\>

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:307](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L307)

Event listener for the specified event _typenames_. Mirrors the core [d3-selection](https://github.com/d3/d3-selection#selection_on) behavior.

###### Returns

`Record`\<`string`, (...`args`: `unknown`[]) => `unknown`\>

###### Example

**By default, listeners apply globally to all objects, however, passing a namespace with the class name gives control over specific elements:**

```ts
new Plot.on("click.Shape", function (d) {
  console.log("data for shape clicked:", d);
}).on("click.Legend", function (d) {
  console.log("data for legend clicked:", d);
});
```

<a id="translate-7"></a>

##### translate()

###### Call Signature

> **translate**(): (`d`: `string`, `locale?`: `string`) => `string`

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:347](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L347)

Defines how informational text strings should be displayed. By default, this function will try to find the string in question (which is the first argument provided to this function) inside of an internally managed translation Object. If you'd like to override to use custom text, simply pass this method your own custom formatting function.

###### Returns

(`d`: `string`, `locale?`: `string`) => `string`

###### Example

**For example, if we wanted to only change the string "Back" and allow all other string to return in English:**

```ts
.translate(function(d) {
return d === "Back" ? "Get outta here" : d;
})
```

<a id="box"></a>

### Box

Defined in: [shapes/Box.ts:266](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/shapes/Box.ts#L266)

Creates SVG box-and-whisker plots based on an array of data, one per group of values.

#### Extends

- [`BaseClass`](#baseclass)

#### Config accessors

Each is a getter/setter: `.key(value)` sets it and returns the instance, `.key()` returns it.

| Accessor             | Type                                                 | Default             | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `backgroundImage`    | `constoraccessor`                                    | —                   | An image drawn inside each box (see `ShapeConfig.backgroundImage`); `rectConfig.backgroundImage` overrides it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `backgroundImageFit` | `constoraccessor`                                    | —                   | How the box's `backgroundImage` fits it: `"cover"` (default) or `"contain"`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `boxMax`             | `string \| function`                                 | —                   | Precomputed boxes: each row's upper whisker end, a data key or accessor in the same units as the value axis's `x` or `y`. See `boxMedian`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `boxMedian`          | `string \| function`                                 | —                   | Precomputed boxes: each row's median, a data key or accessor in the same units as the value axis's `x` or `y`. Setting it, `boxMin`, `boxQ1`, `boxQ3`, or `boxMax` makes each row one box drawn from those values, with nothing computed and `whiskerMode` unused. All five are needed (a warning names any left unset), and a row whose values aren't all numbers draws no box. |
| `boxMin`             | `string \| function`                                 | —                   | Precomputed boxes: each row's lower whisker end. See `boxMedian`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `boxOutliers`        | `string \| function`                                 | —                   | Precomputed boxes: each row's outliers, a data key or accessor returning an array of values drawn past the whiskers. See `boxMedian`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `boxQ1`              | `string \| function`                                 | —                   | Precomputed boxes: each row's lower quartile, where the box starts. See `boxMedian`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `boxQ3`              | `string \| function`                                 | —                   | Precomputed boxes: each row's upper quartile, where the box ends. See `boxMedian`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `fill`               | `constoraccessor`                                    | —                   | Each box's fill, resolved against its merged datum (white when unset); `rectConfig.fill` overrides it. Outliers take it too, resolved against each observation, and the median line defaults to black or white, whichever contrasts with it.                                                                                                                                     |
| `id`                 | `constoraccessor`                                    | —                   | Each box's id, read from its first row; keys every part the box draws. Defaults to the box's x (vertical) or y (horizontal) value.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `orient`             | `constoraccessor`                                    | `function`          | Orientation: "vertical" or "horizontal".                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `outlier`            | `constoraccessor`                                    | `function`          | The shape each outlier draws as: `"Circle"` (default) or `"Rect"`, or `false` to draw no point. An accessor receives each outlier's observation (a precomputed box's row). In BoxWhisker, the value axis leaves out the outliers it hides and reaches only as far as the whiskers.                                                                                               |
| `rectWidth`          | `constoraccessor`                                    | `function`          |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `stroke`             | `constoraccessor`                                    | —                   | Each box's outline color, resolved against its merged datum (black when unset); `rectConfig.stroke` overrides it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `texture`            | `constoraccessor`                                    | —                   | Texture (per textures.js) filling each box; `rectConfig.texture` overrides it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `textureDefault`     | `record`                                             | —                   | Default texture config merged into the box's texture.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `whiskerMode`        | `string \| number \| array.&lt;string \| number&gt;` | `["tukey","tukey"]` | Whisker mode: single mode string/number or [low, high] pair.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `x`                  | `constoraccessor`                                    | `function`          |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `y`                  | `constoraccessor`                                    | `function`          |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:283](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L283)

Overrides the default colors used when assigning fills from data and choosing legible text colors: `dark` and `light` (the text colors picked for contrast against a background), `missing` (null/undefined values), `on`/`off` (`true`/`false` values), `sequential` (the anchor hue for magnitude ramps), and `scale` (the categorical palette, given as a d3 ordinal scale or an array of colors). Keys are merged into the current defaults, and a Viz passes its overrides down to the shapes and components it draws.

###### Returns

`ColorDefaults`

###### Example

```ts
new Treemap().colorDefaults({
  dark: "#222",
  light: "#fff",
  scale: ["#1b9e77", "#d95f02", "#7570b3"],
});
```

The locale used for all text and number formatting. Supports the locales defined in [d3plus-format](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus-format/blob/master/src/locale.js). The locale can be a complex Object, a locale code (like "en-US"), or a 2-digit language code (like "en").         grouping: [3],

```ts
          thousands: ",",
          decimal: "."

```

##### toScene()

> **toScene**(): `GroupNode`

Defined in: [shapes/Box.ts:430](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/shapes/Box.ts#L430)

Compute-mode scene aggregation. When Box is rendered with
`renderMode("compute")`, the inner Rect/Whisker/Circle/etc.
shapes are mounted scene-only (no parent <g>); their `toScene()`
methods produce GroupNodes that we wrap into a single Box-level
group so collectComputed(boxInstance) yields the union. Each part
names its box in `owners`, so `"click.Box"` handlers fire on it.

###### Returns

`GroupNode`

<a id="translate-8"></a>

##### translate()

###### Call Signature

> **translate**(): (`d`: `string`, `locale?`: `string`) => `string`

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:347](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L347)

Defines how informational text strings should be displayed. By default, this function will try to find the string in question (which is the first argument provided to this function) inside of an internally managed translation Object. If you'd like to override to use custom text, simply pass this method your own custom formatting function.

###### Returns

(`d`: `string`, `locale?`: `string`) => `string`

###### Example

**For example, if we wanted to only change the string "Back" and allow all other string to return in English:**

```ts
.translate(function(d) {
return d === "Back" ? "Get outta here" : d;
})
```

Overrides the default colors used when assigning fills from data and choosing legible text colors: `dark` and `light` (the text colors picked for contrast against a background), `missing` (null/undefined values), `on`/`off` (`true`/`false` values), `sequential` (the anchor hue for magnitude ramps), and `scale` (the categorical palette, given as a d3 ordinal scale or an array of colors). Keys are merged into the current defaults, and a Viz passes its overrides down to the shapes and components it draws.

###### Returns

`ColorDefaults`

```ts
new Treemap().colorDefaults({
```

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:347](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L347)

Defines how informational text strings should be displayed. By default, this function will try to find the string in question (which is the first argument provided to this function) inside of an internally managed translation Object. If you'd like to override to use custom text, simply pass this method your own custom formatting function.

###### Returns

(`d`: `string`, `locale?`: `string`) => `string`

###### Example

**For example, if we wanted to only change the string "Back" and allow all other string to return in English:**

```ts
.translate(function(d) {
return d === "Back" ? "Get outta here" : d;
})
```

Creates an SVG color scale based on an array of data.

#### Extends

- [`BaseClass`](#baseclass)

#### Config accessors

Each is a getter/setter: `.key(value)` sets it and returns the instance, `.key()` returns it.

| `bucketAxis`      | `boolean`                        | `false`    |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `bucketFormat`    | `function`                       | `function` | Formats the label for each bucket in a bucket-type scale ("jenks", "quantile", …). Each is a value or a function of the hovered value. |

##### axisConfig()

###### Call Signature

> **axisConfig**(): `Record`\<`string`, `unknown`\>

Defined in: [components/ColorScale/ColorScale.ts:287](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/components/ColorScale/ColorScale.ts#L287)

The ColorScale is constructed by combining an Axis for the ticks/labels and a Rect for the actual color box (or multiple boxes, as in a jenks scale). Because of this, there are separate configs for the Axis class used to display the text (axisConfig) and the Rect class used to draw the color breaks (rectConfig). This method acts as a pass-through to the config method of the Axis.

##### className()

> **className**(): `string` \| `string`[] \| `undefined`

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:250](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L250)

CSS classes added to the outermost element this chart or component draws
into, next to its fixed d3plus classes, so page CSS can target it: a
chart's root `<svg class="d3plus-viz">` (its `<canvas>` with the Canvas
renderer) and a standalone component's `<svg>`. Takes a space-separated
string or an array. A new value replaces the classes the previous one
added; unset adds none. Tooltips take their own `tooltipConfig.className`.

###### Returns

`string` \| `string`[] \| `undefined`

###### Example

```ts
new d3plus.BarChart().className("revenue-chart dark");
```

<a id="colordefaults-10"></a>

##### colorDefaults()

###### Call Signature

> **colorDefaults**(): `ColorDefaults`

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:283](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L283)

Overrides the default colors used when assigning fills from data and choosing legible text colors: `dark` and `light` (the text colors picked for contrast against a background), `missing` (null/undefined values), `on`/`off` (`true`/`false` values), `sequential` (the anchor hue for magnitude ramps), and `scale` (the categorical palette, given as a d3 ordinal scale or an array of colors). Keys are merged into the current defaults, and a Viz passes its overrides down to the shapes and components it draws.

###### Returns

`ColorDefaults`

###### Example

```ts
new Treemap().colorDefaults({
  dark: "#222",
  light: "#fff",
  scale: ["#1b9e77", "#d95f02", "#7570b3"],
});
```

##### locale()

###### Call Signature

> **locale**(): `string`

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:231](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L231)

The locale used for all text and number formatting. Supports the locales defined in [d3plus-format](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus-format/blob/master/src/locale.js). The locale can be a complex Object, a locale code (like "en-US"), or a 2-digit language code (like "en"). If a 2-digit code is provided, the "findLocale" function is used to identify the most approximate locale.

###### Returns

`string`

###### Example

```ts
{
        separator: "",
        suffixes: ["y", "z", "a", "f", "p", "n", "\u00b5", "m", "", "k", "M", "B", "t", "q", "Q", "Z", "Y"],
        grouping: [3],
        delimiters: {
          thousands: ",",
          decimal: "."
        },
        currency: ["$", ""]
      }
```

##### on()

> **on**(): `Record`\<`string`, (...`args`: `unknown`[]) => `unknown`\>

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:307](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L307)

Event listener for the specified event _typenames_. Mirrors the core [d3-selection](https://github.com/d3/d3-selection#selection_on) behavior.

###### Returns

`Record`\<`string`, (...`args`: `unknown`[]) => `unknown`\>

###### Example

**By default, listeners apply globally to all objects, however, passing a namespace with the class name gives control over specific elements:**

```ts
new Plot.on("click.Shape", function (d) {
  console.log("data for shape clicked:", d);
}).on("click.Legend", function (d) {
  console.log("data for legend clicked:", d);
});
```

<a id="toscene-9"></a>

##### toScene()

> **toScene**(): `GroupNode`

Defined in: [components/ColorScale/ColorScale.ts:240](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/components/ColorScale/ColorScale.ts#L240)

Produces a backend-agnostic scene graph for this ColorScale with no DOM
dependency. The discrete variant (jenks/buckets/quantile) delegates to the
internal Legend's toScene(); the gradient variant composes the Rect, Axis,
and label TextBox scenes. The scaleGroup's translate (set by the chart's
colorScale feature on `g.d3plus-viz-colorScale`) is read off `_select` so
the content lands at its on-screen position.

A smooth (non-bucketed) gradient paints its Rect with a `gradient:<json>`
fill token (see renderGradientStops); the backend materializes it into a
`<linearGradient>` (SVG) or a CanvasGradient (Canvas). Bucketed gradients
and the discrete variant use concrete per-bucket fills.

###### Returns

`GroupNode`

##### translate()

###### Call Signature

> **translate**(): (`d`: `string`, `locale?`: `string`) => `string`

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:347](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L347)

Defines how informational text strings should be displayed. By default, this function will try to find the string in question (which is the first argument provided to this function) inside of an internally managed translation Object. If you'd like to override to use custom text, simply pass this method your own custom formatting function.

###### Returns

(`d`: `string`, `locale?`: `string`) => `string`

###### Example

**For example, if we wanted to only change the string "Back" and allow all other string to return in English:**

```ts
.translate(function(d) {
return d === "Back" ? "Get outta here" : d;
})
```
