<a id="image"></a>

### Image

Defined in: [shapes/Image.ts:39](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/shapes/Image.ts#L39)

Creates SVG images based on an array of data.

#### Examples

**a sample row of data**

```ts
var data = {url: "file.png", width: "100", height: "50"};
```

**passed to the generator**

```ts
new Image().data([data]).render();
```

**creates the following**

```ts
<image class="d3plus-Image" opacity="1" href="file.png" width="100" height="50" x="0" y="0"></image>
```

**this is shorthand for the following**

```ts
image().data([data])();
```

**which also allows a post-draw callback function**

```ts
image().data([data])(function () {
  alert("draw complete!");
});
```

#### Config accessors

Each is a getter/setter: `.key(value)` sets it and returns the instance, `.key()` returns it.

| Accessor        | Type                  | Default    | Description                                                 |
| --------------- | --------------------- | ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `duration`      | `number`              | `600`      |                                                             |
| `height`        | `constoraccessor`     | `function` |                                                             |
| `id`            | `accessorfn`          | `function` |                                                             |
| `opacity`       | `constoraccessor`     | `function` |                                                             |
| `pointerEvents` | `constoraccessor`     | `function` |                                                             |
| `renderMode`    | `"full" \| "compute"` | `"full"`   | "full" runs the DOM enter/update/exit; "compute" skips DOM. |
| `url`           | `accessorfn`          | `function` | URL accessor returning the image src.                       |
| `width`         | `constoraccessor`     | `function` |                                                             |
| `x`             | `constoraccessor`     | `function` |                                                             |
| `y`             | `constoraccessor`     | `function` |                                                             |

Overrides the default colors used when assigning fills from data and choosing legible text colors: `dark` and `light` (the text colors picked for contrast against a background), `missing` (null/undefined values), `on`/`off` (`true`/`false` values), `sequential` (the anchor hue for magnitude ramps), and `scale` (the categorical palette, given as a d3 ordinal scale or an array of colors). Keys are merged into the current defaults, and a Viz passes its overrides down to the shapes and components it draws.

###### Returns

`ColorDefaults`

###### Example

```ts
new Treemap().colorDefaults({
  dark: "#222",
  light: "#fff",
  scale: ["#1b9e77", "#d95f02", "#7570b3"],
});
```

Event listener for the specified event _typenames_. Mirrors the core [d3-selection](https://github.com/d3/d3-selection#selection_on) behavior.

###### Example

**By default, listeners apply globally to all objects, however, passing a namespace with the class name gives control over specific elements:**

```ts
new Plot.on("click.Shape", function (d) {
  console.log("data for shape clicked:", d);
}).on("click.Legend", function (d) {
  console.log("data for legend clicked:", d);
});
```

<a id="translate-11"></a>

##### translate()

###### Call Signature

> **translate**(): (`d`: `string`, `locale?`: `string`) => `string`

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:347](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L347)

Defines how informational text strings should be displayed. By default, this function will try to find the string in question (which is the first argument provided to this function) inside of an internally managed translation Object. If you'd like to override to use custom text, simply pass this method your own custom formatting function.

###### Returns

(`d`: `string`, `locale?`: `string`) => `string`

###### Example

**For example, if we wanted to only change the string "Back" and allow all other string to return in English:**

```ts
.translate(function(d) {
return d === "Back" ? "Get outta here" : d;
})
```

CSS classes added to the outermost element this chart or component draws
into, next to its fixed d3plus classes, so page CSS can target it: a
chart's root `<svg class="d3plus-viz">` (its `<canvas>` with the Canvas
renderer) and a standalone component's `<svg>`. Takes a space-separated
string or an array. A new value replaces the classes the previous one
added; unset adds none. Tooltips take their own `tooltipConfig.className`.

###### Returns

`string` \| `string`[] \| `undefined`

###### Example

```ts
new d3plus.BarChart().className("revenue-chart dark");
```

<a id="colordefaults-12"></a>

##### colorDefaults()

###### Call Signature

> **colorDefaults**(): `ColorDefaults`

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:283](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L283)

Overrides the default colors used when assigning fills from data and choosing legible text colors: `dark` and `light` (the text colors picked for contrast against a background), `missing` (null/undefined values), `on`/`off` (`true`/`false` values), `sequential` (the anchor hue for magnitude ramps), and `scale` (the categorical palette, given as a d3 ordinal scale or an array of colors). Keys are merged into the current defaults, and a Viz passes its overrides down to the shapes and components it draws.

###### Returns

`ColorDefaults`

###### Example

```ts
new Treemap().colorDefaults({
  dark: "#222",
  light: "#fff",
  scale: ["#1b9e77", "#d95f02", "#7570b3"],
});
```

###### Inherited from

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:231](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L231)

The locale used for all text and number formatting. Supports the locales defined in [d3plus-format](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus-format/blob/master/src/locale.js). The locale can be a complex Object, a locale code (like "en-US"), or a 2-digit language code (like "en"). If a 2-digit code is provided, the "findLocale" function is used to identify the most approximate locale.

###### Returns

`string`

###### Example

```ts
{
        separator: "",
        suffixes: ["y", "z", "a", "f", "p", "n", "\u00b5", "m", "", "k", "M", "B", "t", "q", "Q", "Z", "Y"],
        grouping: [3],
        delimiters: {
          thousands: ",",
          decimal: "."
        },
        currency: ["$", ""]
      }
```

```ts
});
```

<a id="translate-12"></a>

##### translate()

###### Call Signature

> **translate**(): (`d`: `string`, `locale?`: `string`) => `string`

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:347](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L347)

Defines how informational text strings should be displayed. By default, this function will try to find the string in question (which is the first argument provided to this function) inside of an internally managed translation Object. If you'd like to override to use custom text, simply pass this method your own custom formatting function.

###### Returns

(`d`: `string`, `locale?`: `string`) => `string`

###### Example

**For example, if we wanted to only change the string "Back" and allow all other string to return in English:**

```ts
.translate(function(d) {
return d === "Back" ? "Get outta here" : d;
})
```

CSS classes added to the outermost element this chart or component draws
into, next to its fixed d3plus classes, so page CSS can target it: a
chart's root `<svg class="d3plus-viz">` (its `<canvas>` with the Canvas
renderer) and a standalone component's `<svg>`. Takes a space-separated
string or an array. A new value replaces the classes the previous one
added; unset adds none. Tooltips take their own `tooltipConfig.className`.

###### Returns

`string` \| `string`[] \| `undefined`

###### Example

<a id="colordefaults-13"></a>

##### colorDefaults()

###### Call Signature

> **colorDefaults**(): `ColorDefaults`

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:283](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L283)

Overrides the default colors used when assigning fills from data and choosing legible text colors: `dark` and `light` (the text colors picked for contrast against a background), `missing` (null/undefined values), `on`/`off` (`true`/`false` values), `sequential` (the anchor hue for magnitude ramps), and `scale` (the categorical palette, given as a d3 ordinal scale or an array of colors). Keys are merged into the current defaults, and a Viz passes its overrides down to the shapes and components it draws.

###### Returns

`ColorDefaults`

###### Example

```ts
new Treemap().colorDefaults({
  dark: "#222",
  light: "#fff",
  scale: ["#1b9e77", "#d95f02", "#7570b3"],
});
```

##### translate()

###### Call Signature

> **translate**(): (`d`: `string`, `locale?`: `string`) => `string`

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:347](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L347)

Defines how informational text strings should be displayed. By default, this function will try to find the string in question (which is the first argument provided to this function) inside of an internally managed translation Object. If you'd like to override to use custom text, simply pass this method your own custom formatting function.

###### Returns

(`d`: `string`, `locale?`: `string`) => `string`

###### Example

**For example, if we wanted to only change the string "Back" and allow all other string to return in English:**

```ts
.translate(function(d) {
return d === "Back" ? "Get outta here" : d;
})
```

<a id="plot"></a>

### Plot

Defined in: [charts/Plot/index.ts:70](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/charts/Plot/index.ts#L70)

Creates an x/y plot based on an array of data.

#### Extends

- [`Viz`](#viz)

#### Config accessors

Each is a getter/setter: `.key(value)` sets it and returns the instance, `.key()` returns it. Also accepts the config accessors of [`Viz`](#viz).

| Accessor            | Type                                                                                            | Default    | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `axisHover`         | `boolean \| "x" \| "y"`                                                                         | `true`     | Whether hovering a Plot's mark draws a dashed guide from its point to each axis and a badge on that axis with the point's value there, formatted as the tooltip formats that axis's values (the axis's `tickFormat` when set). `"x"` or `"y"` draws them for that direction only (each including its secondary axis). A bar is badged on its value axis only. With a discrete axis, the shared tooltip's crosshair is that axis's guide, and the value axis follows the hovered series' point (or the one nearest the pointer). Defaults to `true` (`"x"` on BumpChart, whose y axes label series rather than values, and on Streamgraph, whose y positions name no values).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `axisHoverConfig`   | `object`                                                                                        | `{…}`      | Styles the `axisHover` guides and badges. `guideConfig` takes `stroke` (the hovered mark's color by default), `strokeWidth` (default `1`), `strokeDasharray` (default `"4 3"`), and `strokeOpacity`. `badgeConfig` takes `fill` (the hovered mark's color by default), `fontColor` (a color contrasting the fill by default), `fontFamily`, `fontSize` (default `12`), `fontWeight` (default `400`), `padding` around the text (default `4`), and `rx` corner radius (default `2`). Each is a value or a `(d, i) => value` accessor of the hovered data row.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `barPadding`        | `number`                                                                                        | `0`        | Padding between bars in pixels.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `baselineBreak`     | `boolean`                                                                                       | —          | When the domain of a linear value axis stops short of the `baseline` (e.g. `[1100, 2100]` with a baseline of `0`), keeps the baseline as the axis's end tick and breaks the axis between it and the domain: a short stretch of axis holds the baseline tick and two tilted marks with a gap in the axis line, then the domain spans the rest. Style it with the axis's `baselineBreakConfig`. In a Plot it applies to a user-supplied value domain (`yDomain`/`yConfig.domain`, or the x versions for horizontal charts), and bars and areas start at the baseline tick, with the break's gap cut across them (`baselineBreakConfig`'s `mask`); turned off, a `yDomain` stretches to reach the baseline while a `yConfig.domain` is kept and cuts its bars off at the axis. Defaults to `true` for the Plots whose marks grow from `0`, such as BarChart, AreaPlot, Histogram, and Lollipop (each chart lists its own default), and `false` for other Plots and a standalone Axis.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `connectGaps`       | `connectgaps`                                                                                   | `true`     | How a line crosses a missing value: a step of the discrete axis that another line has and this one skips, or a row whose value is `null` or `NaN`. `true` (the default) or `"solid"` draws the line straight on through it. `false` breaks the line there, leaving the gap empty. `"dashed"` breaks the line and bridges the gap with a short dash (`"2 4"`) in the line's color, distinct from a forecast's longer dash. An object styles the bridge: `stroke` (default the line's color), `strokeDasharray` (default `"2 4"`; `false` for a solid bridge), `strokeWidth` (default the line's width), and `opacity` (default `1`). A bridge follows the line's curve, since it is drawn along the same path, and is decoration only: it has no tooltip, takes no keyboard focus, and a shared tooltip at a missing step lists no value for that line. Confidence bands are clipped to the stretches between gaps. A point with a gap on both sides draws no line of its own, so turn on `lineMarkers` to show it. Areas, including stacked ones, are drawn as before.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `fillBetween`       | `boolean \| [string\|number, string\|number] \| array.&lt;[string\|number, string\|number]&gt;` | `false`    | Fills the area between two series' lines, in the color of whichever series is higher, switching color where the lines cross: `true` fills between the first two series, `[a, b]` between the series with ids `a` and `b`, and a list of `[a, b]` pairs fills between each pair. The fill follows the lines' curve and leaves pointer events to the lines. Defaults to `false`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `fillBetweenConfig` | `record`                                                                                        | `{…}`      | Area styles for `fillBetween` (default `{fillOpacity: 0.25}`). Style accessors receive a data row of whichever series is higher, with `above` and `below` keys naming the higher and lower series, so a `fill` accessor can color the A > B and B > A regions apart. Like a confidence band, the fill takes `texture`, `textureDefault`, `backgroundImage`, and `backgroundImageFit` from `shapeConfig` (or `shapeConfig.Area`), so a texture accessor that picks a series textures the regions where that series is higher; set them here to style the fill alone, or to `false` to keep it plain.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `forecast`          | `boolean \| number \| string \| date \| function`                                               | —          | Marks a forecast: the stretch of the discrete axis after it gets a shaded backdrop, a rule at its start, and a translated "Forecast" label, and each line's forecast stretch is dashed (see `forecastConfig`). A function flags the forecast rows (e.g. `d => d.Type === "Predicted"`): each line is dashed from its last unflagged point, or throughout when every row is flagged, and the backdrop starts at the earliest of those. `"auto"` (or `true`) flags the rows whose `confidence` bounds spread away from their line. A discrete-axis value (a date or year on a time axis) starts the forecast there. Unset (the default), only a trend line projection (`trendLineConfig.projection`) is marked, from the last fitted value; `false` marks nothing, not even a projection. On bar charts the backdrop starts at the edge of the first forecast bar, and bars keep their own styles. Defaults to `"auto"` on a FanChart.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `forecastConfig`    | `record`                                                                                        | `{…}`      | Styles for the `forecast` marker: the backdrop's `fill` and `fillOpacity` (default `0.05`; `fill: false` hides it), the rule's `stroke`, `strokeWidth` (`1`), `strokeOpacity` (`0.4`), and `strokeDasharray` (`"4 4"`; `stroke: false` hides it), the label's text as `label` (default "Forecast", translated; `false` hides it) with `fontColor`, `fontFamily`, `fontSize` (`12`), `fontWeight`, and `fontOpacity` (`0.7`), and `lineDasharray`, the dash pattern of each line's forecast stretch (default `"6 4"`; `false` keeps lines solid). Colors default to the chart's text color for its background. The backdrop is chart chrome with no data row, so `shapeConfig.texture` and `shapeConfig.backgroundImage` leave it plain; give it its own `texture` (a textures.js name or config, drawn in the backdrop's color over its shade at `textureOpacity`, default `0.3`, with `textureDefault`) or `backgroundImage` (a URL, fit by `backgroundImageFit`, `"cover"` or `"contain"`). Both are off by default.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `lineLabelConfig`   | `linelabelconfig`                                                                               | `{…}`      | Options for `lineLabels`. `value: true` adds the line's value at each labeled end after the series name (e.g. "Brazil 37%"), formatted as the y axis formats its ticks (its `tickFormat` when set). `valueFormat` formats it instead, as a function of the value, the row it belongs to, and the row's index. Defaults to `{value: false}`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `lineLabels`        | `linelabelssetting`                                                                             | —          | Labels each line of a line chart with its series name, just past the line's ends: `true` or `"end"` labels the right end, `"start"` the left end, and `"both"` both ends. A function of each row returns any of these (or `false`) to choose per series. The plot leaves room for the labels on the side they sit, at most a quarter of its width past the y axis per side; a label wider than that drops its value, then shortens its name with an ellipsis, then hides. Labels that would overlap are moved apart, each side on its own, with a dotted connector back to their line; when the plot is too short for them all, the last that fits reads "+N more". `lineLabelConfig` adds each end's value to its label.<br><br>`"along"` writes each series name along its own line instead, following its curve: on the stretch that bends and slopes least and stays clear of the other lines and labels, reading upright whichever way the line runs. A line with no clear stretch for its name goes unlabeled, a chart (or small-multiples panel) with a single line names none, and the plot leaves no room past the lines for these labels. The Line shape's `labelConfig` sets their `fontSize`, `fontFamily`, and `fontWeight`. When every line gets a name, the default legend hides (a `legend` of your own always wins). LinePlot defaults to `"along"`; other charts default to no labels. |
| `referenceBands`    | `array.&lt;referencebandconfig&gt;`                                                             | `[]`       | Plot: shaded spans across the plot between two values, such as a recession or a target range. Give each entry `x` (a vertical band) or `y` (a horizontal one) as `[start, end]` in data units (numbers, dates, or categories; on a category axis the band covers each end category's whole slot), or `x2`/`y2` for the secondary axes, or `ref: "plot"` for fractions of the plot area. An optional `label` sits inside the band's top-left corner (`labelPosition: "end"` for the top-right), with `fontColor`, `fontFamily`, `fontSize`, `fontWeight`, `lineHeight`, and `maxWidth`. The fill defaults to the chart's text color at `fillOpacity` `0.08`, so it reads on light and dark themes; `stroke`, `strokeWidth`, and `strokeOpacity` add edges. On a continuous or time axis the band's ends count toward the axis domain, widening it to show the whole band (an end set by `xDomain`/`yDomain`/`x2Domain`/`y2Domain` or the axis config's `domain` stays put). Each entry expands into a `"ReferenceBand"` annotation (see `annotations`) behind the data (`layer: "front"` to draw it over; its label always draws above), which follows zoom and never responds to the pointer or keyboard. A label that would cover a data label or another reference label moves to the band's other corners or along its length, inside the plot, and is hidden when no spot is free.                   |

<a id="annotations"></a>

##### annotations()

> **annotations**(`_?`: `unknown`): [`Plot`](#plot) \| `unknown`[]

Defined in: [charts/Plot/index.ts:397](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/charts/Plot/index.ts#L397)

Allows drawing custom shapes to be used as annotations in the provided x/y plot. This method accepts custom config objects for the [Shape](http://d3plus.org/docs/#Shape) class, either a single config object or an array of config objects. Each config object requires an additional parameter, the "shape", which denotes which [Shape](http://d3plus.org/docs/#Shape) sub-class to use ([Rect](http://d3plus.org/docs/#Rect), [Line](http://d3plus.org/docs/#Line), etc).

Additionally, each config object can also contain an optional "layer" key, which defines whether the annotations will be displayed in "front" or in "back" of the primary visualization shapes. This value defaults to "back" if not present ("front" for callouts).

Three more kinds draw chart notes: `"Callout"` anchors wrapped text in a box at each data row's `x`/`y` (in data units, or plot-area fractions with `xRef`/`yRef: "plot"`), offset by `dx`/`dy` pixels and joined to its anchor by a connector ending in an arrowhead or dot (see `CalloutAnnotation`); `"ReferenceLine"` and `"ReferenceBand"` draw what `referenceLines` and `referenceBands` entries expand into. All annotations follow zoom and never respond to the pointer or keyboard.

###### Parameters

| `_?`      | `unknown` |

<a id="baseline"></a>

##### baseline()

> **baseline**(`_?`: `number`): `number` \| [`Plot`](#plot) \| `undefined`

Defined in: [charts/Plot/index.ts:415](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/charts/Plot/index.ts#L415)

Starts the value axis (the x axis for horizontal charts) at a value: `baseline(n)` renders exactly like `yDomain([n])` (or `xDomain([n])`). Bars, areas, and stems still grow from the chart's own `0` in the Plots that draw from one (such as BarChart, AreaPlot, Histogram, and Lollipop), so with `baselineBreak` on (their default) the axis breaks back to a `0` tick and bars run through the break, with its gap cut across them, and with it off the axis stretches down to `0`. As with `yDomain([n])`, only `n` is pinned: the far end comes from the data and is rounded where the axis would round it with no domain set (left at the data when the axis config's `rounding` is "none"), and marks for values past `n` stop at the axis's edge. When every value sits at or below `n`, it ends the axis instead, like `yDomain([undefined, n])`. A bound given in `yDomain`/`xDomain` wins. Returns the chart's own baseline when none is set.

###### Parameters

| Parameter | Type     |
| --------- | -------- |
| `_?`      | `number` |

###### Returns

`number` \| [`Plot`](#plot) \| `undefined`

<a id="confidence"></a>

##### confidence()

> **confidence**(`_?`: `unknown`): `false` \| [`Plot`](#plot) \| \[`false` \| `ConfidenceAccessor`, `false` \| `ConfidenceAccessor`\] \| `ConfidenceBand`[] \| `undefined`

Defined in: [charts/Plot/index.ts:477](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/charts/Plot/index.ts#L477)

The confidence interval as an array of [lower, upper] bounds. Lines draw it as a shaded band; bars draw an error bar per bar, from the lower to the upper bound with a cap at each end (a stacked bar's bounds keep their distance from its value, measured from the bar's stacked end). Either bound may be `false` for a one-sided interval, and a row without a bound pinches the band onto its line. The value axis widens to fit the bounds, and tooltips list them (see `confidenceConfig.tooltip`). Pass `false` to turn the interval off.

Pass an array of bands, outermost first, to draw nested bands around each line (a fan): each band is a `[lower, upper]` pair or `[lower, upper, label]`, or a `{lower, upper, label}` object, and `confidenceConfig.bandOpacity` shades them from the widest (lightest) to the narrowest (darkest). Tooltips list each band's range under its label ("Band 1", "Band 2", … when unlabeled), and bars draw the first band's error bar.

###### Parameters

| Parameter | Type      |
| --------- | --------- |
| `_?`      | `unknown` |

###### Returns

`false` \| [`Plot`](#plot) \| \[`false` \| `ConfidenceAccessor`, `false` \| `ConfidenceAccessor`\] \| `ConfidenceBand`[] \| `undefined`

###### Example

**Can be called with accessor functions or static keys:**

```ts
var data = {id: "alpha", value: 10, lci: 9, hci: 11};
...
// Accessor functions
.confidence([function(d) { return d.lci }, function(d) { return d.hci }])

// Or static keys
.confidence(["lci", "hci"])

// Or nested bands, outermost first
.confidence([["p5", "p95", "90%"], ["p25", "p75", "50%"]])
```

<a id="confidenceconfig"></a>

##### confidenceConfig()

> **confidenceConfig**(`_?`: `Record`\<`string`, `unknown`\>): `Record`\<`string`, `unknown`\> \| [`Plot`](#plot)

Defined in: [charts/Plot/index.ts:495](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/charts/Plot/index.ts#L495)

Configuration object for shapes rendered as confidence intervals. A line's band is an Area, filled with the line's color at half opacity. A bar's error bar is a Path styled by `stroke` (default a shade darker than the bar), `strokeWidth` (default `2`), `strokeDasharray`, `strokeOpacity`, and `capWidth`: the length of each end cap, in pixels or as a percentage string of the bar's thickness (default `"50%"`). Keys nested under `Area` or `Bar` apply only to that shape's interval. With several bands, `bandOpacity` sets how each band looks where it is the innermost band drawn: an array ramps from the outermost band to the innermost (default `[0.15, 0.6]`), a number gives every band that opacity, and either replaces `fillOpacity`. `tooltip` (default `true`) lists the bounds in tooltips: a "Lower Bound" and "Upper Bound" row for a single mark, and a range after each series' value in a shared tooltip; set it to `false` to leave them out. Accepted keys: any key the Area or Path shape takes at the top level, plus `bandOpacity`, `capWidth`, `tooltip`, `Area` (Area keys), and `Bar` (Path keys and `capWidth`); any other key logs a warning.

| `_?`      | `Record`\<`string`, `unknown`\> |

###### Returns

`Record`\<`string`, `unknown`\> \| [`Plot`](#plot)

###### Example

```ts
.confidenceConfig({Bar: {stroke: "#333", capWidth: 8}, tooltip: false})
```

Defined in: [charts/viz/VizBase.ts:87](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/charts/viz/VizBase.ts#L87)

The primary data array used to draw the visualization. The value passed should be an _Array_ of objects or a _String_ representing a filepath or URL to be loaded. The following filetypes are supported: `csv`, `tsv`, `txt`, and `json`.

If your data URL needs specific headers to be set, an Object with a "url" and "headers" (or any other `fetch` request option) may also be passed. An Object with any other key is a data row, not a request.

To transform the data before it is drawn (for example, a JSON API that returns its headers split from its values), set `dataFormat`. Passing a formatter as a second argument to this method sets `dataFormat`; calling it with only data keeps the current `dataFormat`.

To re-fetch a URL on an interval and redraw when its data changes, set `dataPollingInterval`; each poll runs `dataFormat`.

Defaults to an empty array (`[]`).

###### Parameters

| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `_?`      | `string` \| `DataPoint`[] \| \{ `headers`: `Record`\<`string`, `string`\>; `url`: `string`; \} | The data array or a URL string to load data from. |
| `f?`      | (`data`: `DataPoint`[]) => `Record`\<`string`, `unknown`\> \| `DataPoint`[]                    | Sets `dataFormat`.                                |

Splits the chart into small multiples: a grid of equally sized panels, one per distinct value of this data key or accessor, each drawing the chart for that value's rows. The panels share one legend, color scale, title, and timeline, color each series the same way, and hover, tooltips, and legend clicks apply across all of them. Pass `false` to draw a single chart. See `facetConfig` for the grid's layout and shared scales.

<a id="facetconfig"></a>

##### facetConfig()

###### Call Signature

> **facetConfig**(): [`FacetConfig`](#facetconfig-2)

Defined in: [charts/viz/VizBase.ts:132](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/charts/viz/VizBase.ts#L132)

Configuration for small multiples (see `facet`), merged into the current config:

- `columns` / `rows`: the grid's shape. Chosen by default to make the panels as large as the chart's shape allows.
- `padding`: the space between panels, in pixels (default `20`).
- `sort`: panel order — `"ascending"` (default), `"descending"`, `"data"` (first appearance), a comparator over facet values, or an Array of values.
- `scales`: `"shared"` (default) gives every panel of a chart with axes the same x/y domains; `"independent"` fits each panel to its own rows. Funnel defaults to `"independent"` (each panel sized to its own widest stage); `"shared"` sizes every panel against the widest stage across all panels. PolarArea and RadialBar default to `"independent"` (each panel's rings and ticks fit its own values); `"shared"` gives every panel the same value domain.
- `axes`: with shared scales, `"outer"` (default) labels the axes only along the grid's left and bottom edges; `"all"` labels every panel. An object sets each axis on its own, as in `{x: "all", y: "outer"}`: every panel labels its x axis, only the left column labels its y axis, and the panels' plot areas line up. BumpChart defaults to `"all"`, and Marimekko labels its categories on every panel and its 0–100% share axis only along the outer edge, even with independent scales.
- `title`: a `(value, data) => string` function for each panel's title, or `false` to hide panel titles.
- `titleConfig`: TextBox config for the panel titles (`fontSize`, `fontWeight`, `fontColor`, `textAnchor`, `padding`, …).

###### Returns

[`FacetConfig`](#facetconfig-2)

###### Inherited from

The locale used for all text and number formatting. Supports the locales defined in [d3plus-format](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus-format/blob/master/src/locale.js). The locale can be a complex Object, a locale code (like "en-US"), or a 2-digit language code (like "en"). If a 2-digit code is provided, the "findLocale" function is used to identify the most approximate locale.

```ts
        separator: "",
        suffixes: ["y", "z", "a", "f", "p", "n", "\u00b5", "m", "", "k", "M", "B", "t", "q", "Q", "Z", "Y"],
        grouping: [3],
        delimiters: {
          thousands: ",",
          decimal: "."
        },
        currency: ["$", ""]
      }
```

<a id="stackorder"></a>

##### stackOrder()

Defined in: [charts/Plot/index.ts:661](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/charts/Plot/index.ts#L661)

Sets the order of stacked series, from the bottom of the stack upward.
Accepts:

- a named order: `"descending"` (default) / `"ascending"` by summed
  value, `"key"` / `"keyReverse"` alphabetically by series key,
  `"none"` / `"data"` for input order, or d3's `"insideOut"`,
  `"appearance"`, `"reverse"`;
- an Array of series keys for an explicit order;
- a value accessor, or a `{value, order}` config, to rank series by an
  aggregate of any data field.

Unknown named strings warn and fall back to `"descending"`. The
default legend lists the series in the order they stack, from the
baseline outward. If _value_ is not specified, returns the current
stack order.

##### translate()

###### Call Signature

> **translate**(): (`d`: `string`, `locale?`: `string`) => `string`

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:347](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L347)

Defines how informational text strings should be displayed. By default, this function will try to find the string in question (which is the first argument provided to this function) inside of an internally managed translation Object. If you'd like to override to use custom text, simply pass this method your own custom formatting function.

###### Returns

(`d`: `string`, `locale?`: `string`) => `string`

###### Example

**For example, if we wanted to only change the string "Back" and allow all other string to return in English:**

```ts
.translate(function(d) {
return d === "Back" ? "Get outta here" : d;
})
```

<a id="trendline"></a>

##### trendLine()

> **trendLine**(`_?`: `TrendLineType`): [`Plot`](#plot) \| `TrendLineType`

Defined in: [charts/Plot/index.ts:564](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/charts/Plot/index.ts#L564)

Draws an automatic trend line fit to the plotted data: `true` (or `"linear"`) for a least-squares line, or one of `"exponential"`, `"logarithmic"`, `"power"`, or `"polynomial"`. By default each series gets its own line in its color; see `trendLineConfig` for grouping, a confidence band, and styling. On a chart with a discrete axis, the line runs along that axis, fitting categories by their order. Set to `false` (the default) to remove.

###### Parameters

| Parameter | Type            |
| --------- | --------------- |
| `_?`      | `TrendLineType` |

###### Returns

[`Plot`](#plot) \| `TrendLineType`

<a id="trendlineconfig"></a>

##### trendLineConfig()

> **trendLineConfig**(`_?`: `Record`\<`string`, `unknown`\>): `Record`\<`string`, `unknown`\> \| [`Plot`](#plot)

Defined in: [charts/Plot/index.ts:584](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/charts/Plot/index.ts#L584)

Options for the trend lines drawn by `trendLine`, merged into the current config:

- `group`: `"series"` (default) fits one line per series, colored to match it; `"all"` fits a single line to every point.
- `order`: the polynomial degree when `trendLine` is `"polynomial"` (default `2`).
- `confidence`: draws a confidence band around a linear fit (default `false`).
- `confidenceLevel`: the band's confidence level (default `0.95`).
- `confidenceConfig`: Area shape config for the band (default `{fillOpacity: 0.15}`; fill defaults to the line color).
- `projection`: extends each line past the end of its data, by a number of steps at the data's own spacing (e.g. `5` more years), or to an end value with `{to: 2030}` (default `0`, off). The axis widens to fit, and a linear fit's band becomes a prediction interval that fans out over the projection. Hovering a projected step lists each series' projected value. Ignored on a category axis.
- `projectionConfig`: Line shape config for the projected stretch, over the line's own styles (default `{strokeDasharray: "2 4"}`).
- `tooltip`: shows the fitted equation and R² when hovering a line (default `true`).
- Any other key (`stroke`, `strokeWidth`, `strokeDasharray`, …) styles the Line shape.

Stacked charts always fit one line to the stack totals.

###### Parameters

| Parameter | Type                            |
| --------- | ------------------------------- |
| `_?`      | `Record`\<`string`, `unknown`\> |

###### Returns

`Record`\<`string`, `unknown`\> \| [`Plot`](#plot)

<a id="colordefaults-15"></a>

##### colorDefaults()

###### Call Signature

> **colorDefaults**(): `ColorDefaults`

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:283](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L283)

Overrides the default colors used when assigning fills from data and choosing legible text colors: `dark` and `light` (the text colors picked for contrast against a background), `missing` (null/undefined values), `on`/`off` (`true`/`false` values), `sequential` (the anchor hue for magnitude ramps), and `scale` (the categorical palette, given as a d3 ordinal scale or an array of colors). Keys are merged into the current defaults, and a Viz passes its overrides down to the shapes and components it draws.

###### Returns

`ColorDefaults`

###### Example

```ts
new Treemap().colorDefaults({
```

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:347](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L347)

Defines how informational text strings should be displayed. By default, this function will try to find the string in question (which is the first argument provided to this function) inside of an internally managed translation Object. If you'd like to override to use custom text, simply pass this method your own custom formatting function.

###### Returns

(`d`: `string`, `locale?`: `string`) => `string`

###### Example

**For example, if we wanted to only change the string "Back" and allow all other string to return in English:**

```ts
.translate(function(d) {
return d === "Back" ? "Get outta here" : d;
})
```

<a id="shape"></a>

### Shape

Defined in: [shapes/Shape.ts:123](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/shapes/Shape.ts#L123)

An abstracted class for generating shapes.

#### Extends

- [`BaseClass`](#baseclass)

#### Extended by

- [`Area`](#area)
- [`Bar`](#bar)
- [`Circle`](#circle)
- [`Line`](#line)
- [`Path`](#path)
- [`Rect`](#rect)

#### Config accessors

Each is a getter/setter: `.key(value)` sets it and returns the instance, `.key()` returns it.

| Accessor             | Type                          | Default    | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| -------------------- | ----------------------------- | ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `activeOpacity`      | `number`                      | `0.25`     | Opacity applied to non-active data points (default ~0.25).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `ariaLabel`          | `constoraccessor`             | `function` | ARIA label per datum (accessibility).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `backgroundImage`    | `constoraccessor`             | `function` | An image drawn inside each shape: a URL (or `data:` URI), or an accessor returning one per datum (a falsy value draws none). Every chart's filled data shapes support it; stroked marks like lines and links, and Gauge needles, don't. Set it for all shapes in `shapeConfig`, or for one shape kind under its name (like `shapeConfig.Rect.backgroundImage`). The image is clipped to the shape's outline, sized by `backgroundImageFit`, and drawn over the shape's fill and under its label.                     |
| `backgroundImageFit` | `constoraccessor`             | `function` | How a `backgroundImage` fits its shape: `"cover"` (default) fills the shape's bounding box, cropping the overflow and clipping to the outline; `"contain"` fits the whole image, centered and fully visible, inside the shape's largest inscribed rectangle.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `discrete`           | `"x" \| "y"`                  | —          | Discrete-axis key ("x" \| "y") for charts that flip layout per axis.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `duration`           | `number`                      | `600`      | Animation duration in ms.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `fill`               | `csscolor \| function`        | `function` | Fill color or accessor returning one.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `fillOpacity`        | `constoraccessor`             | `function` | Fill opacity (0..1).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `hitArea`            | `record \| false \| function` | —          | An invisible hover and click target drawn behind each mark: bounds (`x`, `y`, `width`, `height`, relative to the mark's position), or a function returning them per datum. A Line takes a wide transparent stroke along its path. Side-by-side bars in a Plot (a BarChart that isn't stacked, or a Histogram) fill their whole slot by default, from one edge of the plot to the other, so a short bar is as easy to hover as a tall one; `shapeConfig: {Bar: {hitArea: false}}` limits them to the bars themselves. |
| `hoverOpacity`       | `number`                      | `0.5`      | Opacity applied to non-hovered data points.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

<a id="classname-16"></a>

##### className()

###### Call Signature

> **className**(): `string` \| `string`[] \| `undefined`

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:250](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L250)

CSS classes added to the outermost element this chart or component draws
into, next to its fixed d3plus classes, so page CSS can target it: a
chart's root `<svg class="d3plus-viz">` (its `<canvas>` with the Canvas
renderer) and a standalone component's `<svg>`. Takes a space-separated
string or an array. A new value replaces the classes the previous one
added; unset adds none. Tooltips take their own `tooltipConfig.className`.

###### Returns

`string` \| `string`[] \| `undefined`

###### Example

```ts
new d3plus.BarChart().className("revenue-chart dark");
```

###### Inherited from

<a id="colordefaults-16"></a>

##### colorDefaults()

###### Call Signature

> **colorDefaults**(): `ColorDefaults`

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:283](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L283)

Overrides the default colors used when assigning fills from data and choosing legible text colors: `dark` and `light` (the text colors picked for contrast against a background), `missing` (null/undefined values), `on`/`off` (`true`/`false` values), `sequential` (the anchor hue for magnitude ramps), and `scale` (the categorical palette, given as a d3 ordinal scale or an array of colors). Keys are merged into the current defaults, and a Viz passes its overrides down to the shapes and components it draws.

###### Returns

`ColorDefaults`

###### Example

```ts
new Treemap().colorDefaults({
  dark: "#222",
  light: "#fff",
  scale: ["#1b9e77", "#d95f02", "#7570b3"],
});
```

###### Inherited from

[`BaseClass`](#baseclass).[`colorDefaults`](#colordefaults-7)

<a id="locale-16"></a>

##### locale()

###### Call Signature

> **locale**(): `string`

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:231](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L231)

The locale used for all text and number formatting. Supports the locales defined in [d3plus-format](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus-format/blob/master/src/locale.js). The locale can be a complex Object, a locale code (like "en-US"), or a 2-digit language code (like "en"). If a 2-digit code is provided, the "findLocale" function is used to identify the most approximate locale.

###### Returns

`string`

###### Example

```ts
{
        separator: "",
        suffixes: ["y", "z", "a", "f", "p", "n", "\u00b5", "m", "", "k", "M", "B", "t", "q", "Q", "Z", "Y"],
        grouping: [3],
        delimiters: {
          thousands: ",",
          decimal: "."
        },
        currency: ["$", ""]
      }
```

###### Inherited from

<a id="on-16"></a>

##### on()

###### Call Signature

> **on**(): `Record`\<`string`, (...`args`: `unknown`[]) => `unknown`\>

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:307](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L307)

Event listener for the specified event _typenames_. Mirrors the core [d3-selection](https://github.com/d3/d3-selection#selection_on) behavior.

###### Returns

`Record`\<`string`, (...`args`: `unknown`[]) => `unknown`\>

###### Example

**By default, listeners apply globally to all objects, however, passing a namespace with the class name gives control over specific elements:**

```ts
new Plot.on("click.Shape", function (d) {
  console.log("data for shape clicked:", d);
}).on("click.Legend", function (d) {
  console.log("data for legend clicked:", d);
});
```

<a id="translate-16"></a>

##### translate()

###### Call Signature

> **translate**(): (`d`: `string`, `locale?`: `string`) => `string`

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:347](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L347)

Defines how informational text strings should be displayed. By default, this function will try to find the string in question (which is the first argument provided to this function) inside of an internally managed translation Object. If you'd like to override to use custom text, simply pass this method your own custom formatting function.

###### Returns

(`d`: `string`, `locale?`: `string`) => `string`

###### Example

**For example, if we wanted to only change the string "Back" and allow all other string to return in English:**

```ts
.translate(function(d) {
return d === "Back" ? "Get outta here" : d;
})
```

<a id="sizelegend"></a>

### SizeLegend

Defined in: [components/SizeLegend/SizeLegend.ts:80](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/components/SizeLegend/SizeLegend.ts#L80)

A nested-circle legend for a size scale: concentric circles sharing a
bottom tangent, each labeled with the value its radius encodes.

Charts that size marks by a `size` accessor (bubble plots, Geomap points,
Network, Rings) draw one automatically in their bottom-right corner (see
`sizeLegend` and `sizeLegendConfig` on the chart). On its own, give it
any d3 continuous scale that maps values to pixel radii.

#### Example

```ts
new SizeLegend()
  .scale(d3.scaleSqrt().domain([0, 1000]).range([2, 30]))
  .title("Population")
  .select("#container")
  .render();
```

#### Extends

- [`BaseClass`](#baseclass)

#### Config accessors

Each is a getter/setter: `.key(value)` sets it and returns the instance, `.key()` returns it.

| Accessor       | Type                                         | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `labelPadding` | `number`                                     | `4`     | Gap between each leader line and its label, in pixels.                                                                                                                                                         |
| `lineLength`   | `number`                                     | `6`     | Length of the leader lines past the largest circle, in pixels.                                                                                                                                                 |
| `padding`      | `number`                                     | `4`     |                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `scale`        | `constoraccessor`                            | —       | Scale factor (1 = identity).                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `tickFormat`   | `function`                                   | —       | Formats each value's label. Defaults to the locale's abbreviated number format.                                                                                                                                |
| `title`        | `string`                                     | —       | Title above the circles. Defaults to the `size` key when `size` is set to a string.                                                                                                                            |
| `values`       | `number \| array.&lt;number&gt; \| function` | —       | The values to draw circles for: an array of values, how many to pick from the size domain (default 3: its min, max, and a round middle), or a function receiving the `[min, max]` domain and returning values. |

##### colorDefaults()

> **colorDefaults**(): `ColorDefaults`

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:283](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L283)

Overrides the default colors used when assigning fills from data and choosing legible text colors: `dark` and `light` (the text colors picked for contrast against a background), `missing` (null/undefined values), `on`/`off` (`true`/`false` values), `sequential` (the anchor hue for magnitude ramps), and `scale` (the categorical palette, given as a d3 ordinal scale or an array of colors). Keys are merged into the current defaults, and a Viz passes its overrides down to the shapes and components it draws.

###### Returns

`ColorDefaults`

###### Example

```ts
new Treemap().colorDefaults({
  dark: "#222",
  light: "#fff",
  scale: ["#1b9e77", "#d95f02", "#7570b3"],
});
```

> **locale**(): `string`

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:231](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L231)

The locale used for all text and number formatting. Supports the locales defined in [d3plus-format](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus-format/blob/master/src/locale.js). The locale can be a complex Object, a locale code (like "en-US"), or a 2-digit language code (like "en"). If a 2-digit code is provided, the "findLocale" function is used to identify the most approximate locale.

###### Returns

`string`

###### Example

```ts
{
        separator: "",
        suffixes: ["y", "z", "a", "f", "p", "n", "\u00b5", "m", "", "k", "M", "B", "t", "q", "Q", "Z", "Y"],
        grouping: [3],
        delimiters: {
          thousands: ",",
          decimal: "."
        },
        currency: ["$", ""]
      }
```

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:347](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L347)

Defines how informational text strings should be displayed. By default, this function will try to find the string in question (which is the first argument provided to this function) inside of an internally managed translation Object. If you'd like to override to use custom text, simply pass this method your own custom formatting function.

###### Returns

(`d`: `string`, `locale?`: `string`) => `string`

###### Example

**For example, if we wanted to only change the string "Back" and allow all other string to return in English:**

```ts
.translate(function(d) {
return d === "Back" ? "Get outta here" : d;
})
```

###### Inherited from

##### className()

###### Call Signature

> **className**(): `string` \| `string`[] \| `undefined`

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:250](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L250)

CSS classes added to the outermost element this chart or component draws
into, next to its fixed d3plus classes, so page CSS can target it: a
chart's root `<svg class="d3plus-viz">` (its `<canvas>` with the Canvas
renderer) and a standalone component's `<svg>`. Takes a space-separated
string or an array. A new value replaces the classes the previous one
added; unset adds none. Tooltips take their own `tooltipConfig.className`.

###### Returns

`string` \| `string`[] \| `undefined`

###### Example

```ts
new d3plus.BarChart().className("revenue-chart dark");
```

<a id="colordefaults-18"></a>

##### colorDefaults()

###### Call Signature

> **colorDefaults**(): `ColorDefaults`

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:283](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L283)

Overrides the default colors used when assigning fills from data and choosing legible text colors: `dark` and `light` (the text colors picked for contrast against a background), `missing` (null/undefined values), `on`/`off` (`true`/`false` values), `sequential` (the anchor hue for magnitude ramps), and `scale` (the categorical palette, given as a d3 ordinal scale or an array of colors). Keys are merged into the current defaults, and a Viz passes its overrides down to the shapes and components it draws.

###### Returns

`ColorDefaults`

###### Example

```ts
new Treemap().colorDefaults({
  dark: "#222",
  light: "#fff",
  scale: ["#1b9e77", "#d95f02", "#7570b3"],
});
```

###### Inherited from

##### locale()

###### Call Signature

> **locale**(): `string`

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:231](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L231)

The locale used for all text and number formatting. Supports the locales defined in [d3plus-format](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus-format/blob/master/src/locale.js). The locale can be a complex Object, a locale code (like "en-US"), or a 2-digit language code (like "en"). If a 2-digit code is provided, the "findLocale" function is used to identify the most approximate locale.

###### Returns

`string`

###### Example

```ts
{
        separator: "",
        suffixes: ["y", "z", "a", "f", "p", "n", "\u00b5", "m", "", "k", "M", "B", "t", "q", "Q", "Z", "Y"],
        grouping: [3],
        delimiters: {
          thousands: ",",
          decimal: "."
        },
        currency: ["$", ""]
      }
```

Event listener for the specified event _typenames_. Mirrors the core [d3-selection](https://github.com/d3/d3-selection#selection_on) behavior.

**By default, listeners apply globally to all objects, however, passing a namespace with the class name gives control over specific elements:**

```ts

});
```

<a id="translate-18"></a>

##### translate()

###### Call Signature

> **translate**(): (`d`: `string`, `locale?`: `string`) => `string`

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:347](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L347)

Defines how informational text strings should be displayed. By default, this function will try to find the string in question (which is the first argument provided to this function) inside of an internally managed translation Object. If you'd like to override to use custom text, simply pass this method your own custom formatting function.

###### Returns

(`d`: `string`, `locale?`: `string`) => `string`

###### Example

**For example, if we wanted to only change the string "Back" and allow all other string to return in English:**

```ts
.translate(function(d) {
return d === "Back" ? "Get outta here" : d;
})
```

### Timeline

Defined in: [components/Timeline/Timeline.ts:51](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/components/Timeline/Timeline.ts#L51)

Creates an interactive timeline brush component for selecting time periods within a visualization.

#### Extends

- [`Axis`](#axis)

#### Config accessors

Each is a getter/setter: `.key(value)` sets it and returns the instance, `.key()` returns it. Also accepts the config accessors of [`Axis`](#axis).

| Accessor             | Type                                                      | Default     | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `brushCursor`        | `string \| function`                                      | `"pointer"` | The cursor shown over the timeline's brush area, where a click or drag picks periods: a CSS cursor, or a function given how the timeline is drawn (`"ticks"` or `"buttons"`) that returns one. Defaults to `"pointer"`. The handles keep `ew-resize` and the selected range `move`; `handleConfig` and `selectionConfig` take a `cursor` too.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `brushFilter`        | `function`                                                | `function`  | Brush event filter.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `brushing`           | `boolean`                                                 | `true`      |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `brushMax`           | `number`                                                  | —           | The maximum number of ticks (or buttons) a selection can span; unlimited by default. A wider brush is pulled in to it on release, keeping the end being dragged, and a wider starting selection keeps its latest periods. A `brushMax` below `brushMin` rises to it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `brushMin`           | `number`                                                  | `function`  | The minimum number of ticks (or buttons) a selection can span. Helpful for x/y plots where selecting fewer than 2 time periods is undesirable. A narrower brush widens to it on release: a drag keeps the end being dragged (or, with ticks, its first tick), and a click selects the clicked period and the ones after it. A narrower starting selection keeps its latest period, and a chart that starts on its latest period starts on its latest `brushMin` instead. Either way, the selection grows the other way where the timeline runs out. Unused with `brushing: false`. |
| `buttonAlign`        | `"start" \| "middle" \| "end"`                            | `"middle"`  | Toggles the horizontal alignment of the button timeline.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `buttonBehavior`     | `"auto" \| "buttons" \| "ticks"`                          | `"auto"`    | How the timeline draws its periods: `"ticks"` along an axis, `"buttons"` in a row, or `"auto"` (the default), which draws buttons when every label fits and ticks otherwise, and checks again whenever the chart redraws. The timeline's group carries a class naming the result, for page CSS: `d3plus-viz-timeline-ticks` or `d3plus-viz-timeline-buttons` on a chart's `g.d3plus-viz-timeline`, and `d3plus-Timeline-ticks` or `d3plus-Timeline-buttons` on the Timeline's own group.                                                                                           |

| `playButton`         | `boolean`                                                 | `true`      | Determines the visibility of the play button to the left of the timeline, which cycles through the available periods at a rate set by `playButtonInterval`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `playButtonInterval` | `number`                                                  | `1000`      | The interval, in milliseconds, between periods when cycling via the play button. Used only when the chart's `duration` is 0 (no transition); otherwise playback steps once per `duration` so each step animates in full.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

Overrides the default colors used when assigning fills from data and choosing legible text colors: `dark` and `light` (the text colors picked for contrast against a background), `missing` (null/undefined values), `on`/`off` (`true`/`false` values), `sequential` (the anchor hue for magnitude ramps), and `scale` (the categorical palette, given as a d3 ordinal scale or an array of colors). Keys are merged into the current defaults, and a Viz passes its overrides down to the shapes and components it draws.

<a id="labelrotation-5"></a>

##### labelRotation()

###### Call Signature

> **labelRotation**(): `number` \| `boolean` \| `undefined`

Defined in: [components/Axis/Axis.ts:517](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/components/Axis/Axis.ts#L517)

Whether to rotate the axis labels, and by how much. `true` rotates
them -90 degrees and `false` keeps them flat. Left `undefined` (the
default), a horizontal axis of categories rotates its labels when any
label would not fit its share of the axis whole (a word dropped, cut
off, or broken across lines) or would overlap its neighbor: they
slant 30 degrees (-30 on a bottom axis, 30 on a top one), or stand at
-90 when even slanted they would leave more labels cut short or
hidden. A vertical axis never rotates its labels on its own. A number
rotates them by that many degrees (clockwise, so `-45` rises to the
right): each label hangs off the axis from the end of its text
nearest the axis, which sits across from its tick, so on a bottom
axis a negative angle ends each label at its tick and a positive one
starts it there. Angles outside -90 to 90 turn a half turn to read
left to right (`135` draws as `-45`), and `0` keeps the labels flat.
Slanted labels wrap between words onto up to three lines, as many as
fit between neighboring labels, so they reach less far from the
axis. Labels that still overlap once rotated are thinned evenly.

###### Returns

`number` \| `boolean` \| `undefined`

###### Inherited from

[`Axis`](#axis).[`labelRotation`](#labelrotation)

> **labelRotation**(`_`: `number` \| `boolean` \| `undefined`): `this`
