off, or broken across lines) or would overlap its neighbor: they
slant 30 degrees (-30 on a bottom axis, 30 on a top one), or stand at
-90 when even slanted they would leave more labels cut short or
hidden. A vertical axis never rotates its labels on its own. A number
rotates them by that many degrees (clockwise, so `-45` rises to the
right): each label hangs off the axis from the end of its text
nearest the axis, which sits across from its tick, so on a bottom
axis a negative angle ends each label at its tick and a positive one
starts it there. Angles outside -90 to 90 turn a half turn to read
left to right (`135` draws as `-45`), and `0` keeps the labels flat.
Slanted labels wrap between words onto up to three lines, as many as
fit between neighboring labels, so they reach less far from the
axis. Labels that still overlap once rotated are thinned evenly.

<a id="measure-5"></a>

##### measure()

> **measure**(): `this`

Defined in: [components/Axis/Axis.ts:573](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/components/Axis/Axis.ts#L573)

Runs the layout pass only — scale construction, tick selection, label
textWrap, and outerBounds — with **no DOM access**. After it returns,
`outerBounds()` / `_d3Scale` / `_getPosition()` are populated exactly as
they would be after a full `render()`, but no `<svg>`, `<g>`, tick shapes,
or label TextBoxes are created. Answers "how much room will this axis
need?" without rendering; Plot uses it to size its test-axes. Delegates to
the standalone `measureAxis(axis)` in axisLayout.ts, so callers can run
layout without owning an Axis instance.

###### Returns

`this`

Extends the native Axis scene with the Timeline-specific play-button
TextBox.

The brush selection + handles are NOT composed here: d3-brush owns its
own DOM (mounted in `g.brushGroup` and styled by `_brushStyle`), which the
Viz lifts above the scene so it paints on top of the timeline ticks. That
DOM brush is the sole brush visual and interaction layer — drawing a
second copy from the scene only duplicated it at the wrong height (the
full outer bounds rather than the tick band), so the overlay no longer
lined up with the timeline.

###### Call Signature

> **translate**(): (`d`: `string`, `locale?`: `string`) => `string`

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:347](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L347)

Defines how informational text strings should be displayed. By default, this function will try to find the string in question (which is the first argument provided to this function) inside of an internally managed translation Object. If you'd like to override to use custom text, simply pass this method your own custom formatting function.

###### Returns

(`d`: `string`, `locale?`: `string`) => `string`

###### Example

**For example, if we wanted to only change the string "Back" and allow all other string to return in English:**

```ts
.translate(function(d) {
return d === "Back" ? "Get outta here" : d;
})
```

<a id="colordefaults-20"></a>

##### colorDefaults()

###### Call Signature

> **colorDefaults**(): `ColorDefaults`

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:283](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L283)

Overrides the default colors used when assigning fills from data and choosing legible text colors: `dark` and `light` (the text colors picked for contrast against a background), `missing` (null/undefined values), `on`/`off` (`true`/`false` values), `sequential` (the anchor hue for magnitude ramps), and `scale` (the categorical palette, given as a d3 ordinal scale or an array of colors). Keys are merged into the current defaults, and a Viz passes its overrides down to the shapes and components it draws.

###### Returns

`ColorDefaults`

The locale used for all text and number formatting. Supports the locales defined in [d3plus-format](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus-format/blob/master/src/locale.js). The locale can be a complex Object, a locale code (like "en-US"), or a 2-digit language code (like "en"). If a 2-digit code is provided, the "findLocale" function is used to identify the most approximate locale.

        grouping: [3],
        delimiters: {
          thousands: ",",
          decimal: "."

<a id="parent-20"></a>

##### parent()

###### Call Signature

> **parent**(): `HTMLElement` \| `undefined`

Defined in: [components/Tooltip.ts:284](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/components/Tooltip.ts#L284)

Parent element that scopes the tooltip's portal. Default (unset) uses
the global `<div id="d3plus-portal">` appended to `<body>`. When set,
tooltips mount inside a `.d3plus-tooltip-portal` child of the given
element instead — so multiple charts on a page don't fight over the
global portal, and tooltips destroy cleanly when the chart goes away.

Viz auto-sets this when rendering: chart.tooltipClass.parent(chart._select.node().parentNode).

###### Returns

`HTMLElement` \| `undefined`

The position of each tooltip. Can be an HTMLElement to anchor to, a virtual element (any object with a `getBoundingClientRect()` returning a box in client coordinates), a selection string, or coordinate points in reference to the client viewport (not the overall page). An element or box anchors the tooltip's arrow to the middle of its top edge (or its bottom edge when the tooltip flips below).

Defines how informational text strings should be displayed. By default, this function will try to find the string in question (which is the first argument provided to this function) inside of an internally managed translation Object. If you'd like to override to use custom text, simply pass this method your own custom formatting function.

###### Returns

(`d`: `string`, `locale?`: `string`) => `string`

###### Example

**For example, if we wanted to only change the string "Back" and allow all other string to return in English:**

```ts
.translate(function(d) {
return d === "Back" ? "Get outta here" : d;
})
```

Typing it as a coerced `ResolvedSchema` interface is the only way to drop the `any`; until then it stays. | [`BaseClass`](#baseclass).[`schema`](#property-schema-7) | [utils/BaseClass.ts:132](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L132) |

<a id="viz"></a>

### Viz

Defined in: [charts/viz/Viz.ts:67](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/charts/viz/Viz.ts#L67)

The base class every d3plus chart extends. Owns the shared configuration surface (data, groupBy, size and color accessors, title, legend, tooltip, timeline, zoom, table view) and the render lifecycle that each chart type's definition plugs its layout into. Not used directly; see the chart classes (BarChart, Treemap, …).

#### Extends

- `VizBase`

#### Extended by

- [`Plot`](#plot)

#### Config accessors

Each is a getter/setter: `.key(value)` sets it and returns the instance, `.key()` returns it.

Polling waits while the browser tab is hidden or, with `detectVisible`, while the chart is scrolled out of view, and catches up as soon as it is visible again. A failed request keeps the last data, logs one warning per run of failures, and tries again on the next tick. `destroy()`, setting this to `false`, or passing new `data` stops polling. Only `data` is polled, not `links`, `nodes`, or `topojson`. | `labelPosition`                 | `"auto" \| "along" \| "inside" \| "outside" \| function` | `function`              | Where each shape's label goes, as a string for every shape or a `(d, i) => string` accessor of the data row.<br><br>- Ring segments (Donut slices and those of a Pie with an `innerRadius`, Sunburst arcs, Chord groups, and RadialBar tracks): `"along"` runs a segment's name along its arc, following the ring, reading left to right on the bottom half as on the top. `"auto"` picks, segment by segment, whichever reads better: the curve when its arc is long enough for the whole name and it shows it larger than a straight label could (a thin ring), the straight label when that fits as well, and a curve cut short with an ellipsis when nothing else fits. A full Pie (no `innerRadius`) keeps its labels inside straight: its wedges run to a point at the center. On a Pie or Donut (any `innerRadius`, and partial rings such as a half pie), a slice whose label inside can't show its whole name under `"auto"` is labelled outside the ring instead, and `"outside"` labels every slice there: its name and share, horizontal, in the Path `labelConfig`'s font at its `fontSize` (12px by default), in the theme's text color unless `labelConfig.fontColor` sets one, joined to the slice by a thin leader line. These labels stack in a column on the side of the ring their slice faces, wrapping onto a second line between words when their column is narrow; the ring shrinks (its hole with it) to leave room for them, never below 60% of its full radius, and when they don't all fit, the smallest slices' labels are left out (those slices keep their label inside, if any). `"inside"` keeps a Pie or Donut's labels straight inside their slices, and on the other ring segments both `"inside"` and `"outside"` keep the straight labels. A Donut's curves follow the middle of its ring (the rim, when its hole is small), with the slice's share on a smaller second line when there is room. A Sunburst also weighs a label turned along its radius, which suits the narrow arcs of the outer rings. Curved Donut and Sunburst names keep 5px from the ring's edges and at least 0.3em from the segment's ends, at the largest size from the Path `labelConfig`'s `fontSize` (else `fontMax`, 24px by default) down to its `fontMin` (8px). A Chord curves its group names just outside the ring when every name fits along its arc, which leaves the ring more room; otherwise it curves those that fit and turns the rest along their spokes, all at the Path `labelConfig`'s `fontSize` (11px by default). A Radar does the same with its metric names, just outside the web, each between its neighbors' spokes, wrapping a long name onto a second curved line. A RadialBar curves each track's name along the track, inside its bar (or past its end when the bar is too short), when the sweep leaves no room before the start for the straight labels, and at any sweep for `"along"`; when every track is named this way, the default legend hides. Curved text takes the color that contrasts with what lies under it (the theme's ink outside the ring) and dims with its segment on hover. A label with no room is left out. - Bars: `"inside"` or `"outside"` the bar, or `"auto"`, which goes outside when the bar is shorter than half the room along its axis. Stacked bars always label inside. - Circles (scatter and bubble points, Beeswarm points given a `label`, Network nodes, and Geomap coordinate points): `"auto"` keeps a label inside its circle when it fits there at `pointLabelConfig.fontMin` or larger, else moves it beside the circle, else hides it. A Network or Geomap's labels beside their circles stay in the chart area, a Plot's in its plot area. `"inside"` keeps every label inside, shrinking it to fit (a label that can't fit is dropped). `"outside"` always puts it beside the circle. A label goes beside its circle on the side with the most open room: the side facing its Voronoi cell's centroid first, then right, left, top, bottom, and the diagonals. A side is taken only where the label lies mostly in the circle's Voronoi cell, stays in that area, and overlaps no circle and no label placed before it. Larger circles are placed first. A label with no room is hidden; the circle's tooltip and aria-label still name it. Geomap points are labeled by `shapeConfig.Circle.label` when it is set (`false` turns their labels off), else by `label`. Labels are placed when the chart draws: a zoomed Plot places them again for its new scales, while a zoomed Network or Geomap scales them with the picture. - Stacked areas (StackedArea, Streamgraph, and a stacked AreaPlot): `"auto"` or `"along"` runs each series' name along its band's centerline, following its curve, on the stretch where the band is at least the font size plus 4px thick under the whole label and flattest. The text reads upright, in the color that contrasts with the band's fill (or the Area `labelConfig`'s `fontColor`, when you set one), and dims with its band on hover. It starts at the Area `labelConfig`'s `fontSize` (or `fontMax`, else 16px) and shrinks a pixel at a time down to its `fontMin`, but no lower than 8px, before giving up; a band too thin for its name everywhere goes unlabeled. When every band gets a name, the default legend hides (a `legend` of your own always wins, and the legend stays while a series is hidden from it). `"inside"` (or `"outside"`) puts the label in the band's largest box instead. `shapeConfig.Area.label` sets the text, or `false` for none.<br><br>Defaults to `"auto"`. |
| `legend`                        | `boolean \| function`                                    | `function`              | Whether to display the legend. By default, the legend shows when it has more than one entry and each entry stands for a single group (or two groups at most), or when the entries are colored by a category that isn't a `groupBy` level (see `color`), in which case each entry is labelled by its category. Pass `false` to hide it, `true` to always show it, or a `(config, data) => boolean` function to decide. | `legendHistory`                 | `boolean`                                                | `true`                  | Whether legend clicks go on the chart's Back history. A click or shift+click (or Enter or Space on a legend item) that changes what is hidden or solo'd shows the Back button, and Back undoes legend clicks and drill-downs in the order they happened, restoring the legend exactly as it was. A drill-down to a deeper level starts with every group shown, and Back out of it brings back the legend it left. A click that changes nothing adds no step, and new `data` clears the legend's steps along with the legend. Clicking a Sunburst or Icicle center zooms out without undoing the legend clicks made since the zoom. Defaults to `true`; `false` leaves legend clicks off the history, so Back only steps out of drill-downs. | `legendInset`                   | `boolean \| function`                                    | `true`                  | Whether the chart may draw one of its legends inside the empty space around its marks instead of in a margin, for charts that leave open space around their marks, such as Plot and the charts built on it, Network, Pack, Pie, and Geomap; a chart whose marks fill its area, like Treemap, keeps its legends in the margins. After the chart lays out, the size legend is tried first, then the legend, then the colorScale; the first that fits is drawn over a semi-transparent box (see `legendInsetConfig`), and any others keep their margins. Space enclosed by the marks, like the middle of a ring of points, is never used. Only a legend or colorScale whose position is `"auto"` (the default) can move inside; one set to a side stays in that margin. Defaults to `true`; also accepts a function that receives the resolved chart config and returns a boolean. | `theme`                         | `themesetting`                                           | `"auto"`                | The chart's colors. `"auto"` (the default) paints no background and follows the page behind the chart: its chrome text contrasts with the page, its tooltip, table view, and overlays turn dark on a dark page, and it redraws when the page flips between light and dark. `"light"` and `"dark"` paint the theme's background behind the chart (so it reads the same on any page, and in a saved image) and take every chrome color from the theme. An object sets your own tokens on top of the preset its `base` names (`"light"` or `"dark"`), for example `{base: "dark", background: "#123", accent: "#ffd43b"}`. A dark theme also turns color scale ramps around, from a dim tint near the background up to a bright pole (see the `colorScale` tokens). Colors you set in the other config (`titleConfig.fontColor`, `tooltipConfig`, `colorScaleConfig.colorMax`, the `*Style` options, …) win over the theme. ##### className()

###### Call Signature

> **className**(): `string` \| `string`[] \| `undefined`

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:250](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L250)

CSS classes added to the outermost element this chart or component draws
into, next to its fixed d3plus classes, so page CSS can target it: a
chart's root `<svg class="d3plus-viz">` (its `<canvas>` with the Canvas
renderer) and a standalone component's `<svg>`. Takes a space-separated
string or an array. A new value replaces the classes the previous one
added; unset adds none. Tooltips take their own `tooltipConfig.className`.

###### Returns

`string` \| `string`[] \| `undefined`

###### Example

```ts
new d3plus.BarChart().className("revenue-chart dark");
```

<a id="colordefaults-21"></a>

##### colorDefaults()

###### Call Signature

> **colorDefaults**(): `ColorDefaults`

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:283](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L283)

Overrides the default colors used when assigning fills from data and choosing legible text colors: `dark` and `light` (the text colors picked for contrast against a background), `missing` (null/undefined values), `on`/`off` (`true`/`false` values), `sequential` (the anchor hue for magnitude ramps), and `scale` (the categorical palette, given as a d3 ordinal scale or an array of colors). Keys are merged into the current defaults, and a Viz passes its overrides down to the shapes and components it draws.

###### Returns

`ColorDefaults`

###### Example

```ts
new Treemap().colorDefaults({
  dark: "#222",
  light: "#fff",
  scale: ["#1b9e77", "#d95f02", "#7570b3"],
});
```

###### Inherited from

<a id="data-20"></a>

##### data()

> **data**(`_?`: `string` \| `DataPoint`[] \| \{ `headers`: `Record`\<`string`, `string`\>; `url`: `string`; \}, `f?`: (`data`: `DataPoint`[]) => `Record`\<`string`, `unknown`\> \| `DataPoint`[]): `DataPoint`[] \| [`Viz`](#viz)

Defined in: [charts/viz/VizBase.ts:87](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/charts/viz/VizBase.ts#L87)

The primary data array used to draw the visualization. The value passed should be an _Array_ of objects or a _String_ representing a filepath or URL to be loaded. The following filetypes are supported: `csv`, `tsv`, `txt`, and `json`.

If your data URL needs specific headers to be set, an Object with a "url" and "headers" (or any other `fetch` request option) may also be passed. An Object with any other key is a data row, not a request.

To transform the data before it is drawn (for example, a JSON API that returns its headers split from its values), set `dataFormat`. Passing a formatter as a second argument to this method sets `dataFormat`; calling it with only data keeps the current `dataFormat`.

To re-fetch a URL on an interval and redraw when its data changes, set `dataPollingInterval`; each poll runs `dataFormat`.

Defaults to an empty array (`[]`).

###### Parameters

| Parameter | Type                                                                                           | Description                                       |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `_?`      | `string` \| `DataPoint`[] \| \{ `headers`: `Record`\<`string`, `string`\>; `url`: `string`; \} | The data array or a URL string to load data from. |
| `f?`      | (`data`: `DataPoint`[]) => `Record`\<`string`, `unknown`\> \| `DataPoint`[]                    | Sets `dataFormat`.                                |

###### Returns

`DataPoint`[] \| [`Viz`](#viz)

##### facet()

> **facet**(`_?`: `string` \| `false` \| ((`d`: `DataPoint`, `i`: `number`) => `unknown`)): [`Viz`](#viz) \| ((`d`: `DataPoint`, `i`: `number`) => `unknown`) \| `undefined`

Defined in: [charts/viz/VizBase.ts:114](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/charts/viz/VizBase.ts#L114)

Splits the chart into small multiples: a grid of equally sized panels, one per distinct value of this data key or accessor, each drawing the chart for that value's rows. The panels share one legend, color scale, title, and timeline, color each series the same way, and hover, tooltips, and legend clicks apply across all of them. Pass `false` to draw a single chart. See `facetConfig` for the grid's layout and shared scales.

<a id="facetconfig-1"></a>

##### facetConfig()

###### Call Signature

> **facetConfig**(): [`FacetConfig`](#facetconfig-2)

Defined in: [charts/viz/VizBase.ts:132](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/charts/viz/VizBase.ts#L132)

Configuration for small multiples (see `facet`), merged into the current config:

- `columns` / `rows`: the grid's shape. Chosen by default to make the panels as large as the chart's shape allows.
- `padding`: the space between panels, in pixels (default `20`).
- `sort`: panel order — `"ascending"` (default), `"descending"`, `"data"` (first appearance), a comparator over facet values, or an Array of values.
- `scales`: `"shared"` (default) gives every panel of a chart with axes the same x/y domains; `"independent"` fits each panel to its own rows. Funnel defaults to `"independent"` (each panel sized to its own widest stage); `"shared"` sizes every panel against the widest stage across all panels. PolarArea and RadialBar default to `"independent"` (each panel's rings and ticks fit its own values); `"shared"` gives every panel the same value domain.
- `axes`: with shared scales, `"outer"` (default) labels the axes only along the grid's left and bottom edges; `"all"` labels every panel. An object sets each axis on its own, as in `{x: "all", y: "outer"}`: every panel labels its x axis, only the left column labels its y axis, and the panels' plot areas line up. BumpChart defaults to `"all"`, and Marimekko labels its categories on every panel and its 0–100% share axis only along the outer edge, even with independent scales.
- `title`: a `(value, data) => string` function for each panel's title, or `false` to hide panel titles.
- `titleConfig`: TextBox config for the panel titles (`fontSize`, `fontWeight`, `fontColor`, `textAnchor`, `padding`, …).

###### Returns

[`FacetConfig`](#facetconfig-2)

###### Inherited from

`VizBase.facetConfig`

Defines how informational text strings should be displayed. By default, this function will try to find the string in question (which is the first argument provided to this function) inside of an internally managed translation Object. If you'd like to override to use custom text, simply pass this method your own custom formatting function.

Overrides the default colors used when assigning fills from data and choosing legible text colors: `dark` and `light` (the text colors picked for contrast against a background), `missing` (null/undefined values), `on`/`off` (`true`/`false` values), `sequential` (the anchor hue for magnitude ramps), and `scale` (the categorical palette, given as a d3 ordinal scale or an array of colors). Keys are merged into the current defaults, and a Viz passes its overrides down to the shapes and components it draws.

`ColorDefaults`

> **locale**(): `string`

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:231](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L231)

The locale used for all text and number formatting. Supports the locales defined in [d3plus-format](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus-format/blob/master/src/locale.js). The locale can be a complex Object, a locale code (like "en-US"), or a 2-digit language code (like "en"). If a 2-digit code is provided, the "findLocale" function is used to identify the most approximate locale.

###### Returns

`string`

###### Example

```ts
{
        separator: "",
        suffixes: ["y", "z", "a", "f", "p", "n", "\u00b5", "m", "", "k", "M", "B", "t", "q", "Q", "Z", "Y"],
        grouping: [3],
        delimiters: {
          thousands: ",",
          decimal: "."
        },
        currency: ["$", ""]
      }
```

Event listener for the specified event _typenames_. Mirrors the core [d3-selection](https://github.com/d3/d3-selection#selection_on) behavior.

});

<a id="translate-22"></a>

##### translate()

###### Call Signature

> **translate**(): (`d`: `string`, `locale?`: `string`) => `string`

Defined in: [utils/BaseClass.ts:347](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/BaseClass.ts#L347)

Defines how informational text strings should be displayed. By default, this function will try to find the string in question (which is the first argument provided to this function) inside of an internally managed translation Object. If you'd like to override to use custom text, simply pass this method your own custom formatting function.

###### Returns

(`d`: `string`, `locale?`: `string`) => `string`

###### Example

**For example, if we wanted to only change the string "Back" and allow all other string to return in English:**

```ts
.translate(function(d) {
return d === "Back" ? "Get outta here" : d;
})
```

<a id="configwarnings"></a>

### configWarnings()

#### Call Signature

> **configWarnings**(): `boolean`

Defined in: [utils/configWarnings.ts:18](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/configWarnings.ts#L18)

Toggles the console warnings d3plus logs when a class receives a config
property it does not support (like a misspelled key passed to `.config()`
or `shapeConfig`), or a config key names a data field that no row of the
chart's data has (like `y: "vlaue"`). Warnings are on by default and the
setting applies to every chart on the page. With no argument, returns the
current setting.

##### Returns

`boolean`

##### Example

```ts
import {configWarnings} from "@d3plus/core";
configWarnings(false);
```

| Parameter | Type | Description                             |
| --------- | ---- | --------------------------------------- |
| `value`   | `T`  | The value to wrap in a return function. |

#### Returns

() => `T`

#### Examples

**this**

```ts
constant(42);
```

**returns this**

```ts
function() {
return 42;
}
```

column per entry in `dimensions`, one node per category in each column,

color of its rows' category in the `colorBy` column across every column.

Defined in: [charts/BubbleChart/index.ts:53](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/charts/BubbleChart/index.ts#L53)

Creates a bubble chart from an array of data: each row draws as a circle
at its `x` and `y` values, sized by its `size` value. Bubbles are sized by
area (`sizeZero` with a `"sqrt"` `sizeScale`): a value twice as large
draws a bubble with twice the area, and the largest draws at `sizeMax`
pixels in radius. A size legend keys the sizes, larger bubbles are drawn
first so smaller ones stay on top, and each bubble is outlined in the
chart's background color so overlapping bubbles stay distinct.

Creates a dumbbell (range dot) chart from an array of data with one row per
category and series, such as a country's value in 2010 and in 2020. Each
category, read from the axis named by `discrete` (`"y"` by default, for
horizontal dumbbells), draws a circle per row at its value, colored by
`groupBy`, with a connector between the category's smallest and largest
values. Circles are styled by `shapeConfig.Circle` and connectors by
`shapeConfig.Line`; `gapSort` orders the categories by the size of their
gap.

Creates a fan chart from an array of data: a line per series with nested
`confidence` bands around it, outermost first, shaded from the widest
(lightest) to the narrowest (darkest). The bands open from the last point
before they spread away from the line, and the stretch after it is marked
as a forecast: a shaded backdrop, a rule at its start, a "Forecast" label,
and a dashed line (see `forecast` and `forecastConfig`).

Creates a 2D binned density chart from raw observations: each row is a
point at its `x` and `y` values (rows without numeric values are
skipped), and the points are grouped into hexagons (`binShape`) of
`binSize` pixels, colored on the colorScale by how many each holds (or by
`binValue`). Empty bins aren't drawn. `contours` adds density contours,
and `points` draws the observations beneath. `groupBy` names the
observations for `filter` and the legend (off by default), and `facet`
bins each panel on its own, on one shared colorScale.

Creates a lollipop chart from an array of data: each row draws a thin stem
from the baseline (or the value axis's break) to a circle at its value,
with a category axis set by `discrete` (`"x"` draws vertical stems, `"y"`
horizontal ones). Rows sharing a category but differing in `groupBy` sit
side by side, as grouped bars do. Stems are styled by `shapeConfig.Line`
(`stroke`, `strokeWidth`, …) and heads by `shapeConfig.Circle` (`r`,
`fill`, …); a `size` accessor scales the heads and adds a size legend.

Creates a Marimekko (mosaic) chart from an array of data: one bar per
discrete value (`x`), as wide as its `barWidth` (by default its total),
with the bar's `groupBy` segments stacked to 100% of its height. Each
category is named beneath its bar, with the bar's share of the total
width above it (see `barWidthShare`), and tooltips
show each segment's value, its share of the bar, and the bar's width and
share of the total width. Set `stackOffset("none")` to stack absolute
values instead.

<a id="slopechart"></a>

### SlopeChart

Extends [`LinePlot`](#lineplot) — accepts all of its configuration. Adds or overrides these defaults:

| Method            | Default  |
| ----------------- | -------- |
| `axisHover`       | `"x"`    |
| `legend`          | `false`  |

Defined in: [charts/SlopeChart/index.ts:152](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/charts/SlopeChart/index.ts#L152)

Creates a slope chart from an array of data: a LinePlot comparing each
series between two periods, with a line from its first value to its
second. Each line is labeled at both ends with its series name and value
(`lineLabels: "both"` with `lineLabelConfig: {value: true}`), labels that
would overlap are nudged apart on each side, and the value axis hides its
labels, ticks, and gridlines, since the labels carry the values (tooltips
still show them). The x axis shows the periods in the data; with more
than two, every period is drawn and a warning suggests filtering to two.
Markers sit at each end of every line. `slopeColor` colors each line by
whether it rose, fell, or stayed flat. For ranks rather than values, use
a two-period BumpChart, which labels its rank axes with the series names.

<a id="streamgraph"></a>

### Streamgraph

Extends [`StackedArea`](#stackedarea) — accepts all of its configuration. Adds or overrides these defaults:

| Method        | Default        |
| ------------- | -------------- |

Defined in: [charts/Streamgraph/index.ts:57](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/charts/Streamgraph/index.ts#L57)

Creates a streamgraph from an array of data: a StackedArea whose layers
flow around a central baseline instead of rising from zero. Layers stack
with `stackOffset: "silhouette"`, which centers every stack on the same
line, ordered `"insideOut"` (the largest layers in the middle) along
smooth `monotoneX` curves. The value axis hides its labels and gridlines,
since a moving baseline has no zero to read them from; each layer's
thickness carries its value, and tooltips show each value and its share
of the stack. Set `stackOffset("wiggle")` to keep each layer's slope as
steady as it can instead, at the cost of a stream that drifts up or down
as its total changes. Each layer is named along its own stream (see
`labelPosition`).

Defined in: [charts/Waffle/index.ts:182](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/charts/Waffle/index.ts#L182)

Draws a grid of unit cells filled in order by category, each category
getting cells in proportion to its value. By default the grid is 10 × 10,
so each cell is 1% of the total; set `unit` to make each cell a fixed
amount instead. Hover a cell to highlight its whole category.

<a id="waterfall"></a>

### Waterfall

Extends [`BarChart`](#barchart) — accepts all of its configuration. Adds or overrides these defaults:

| Method            | Default |
| ----------------- | ------- |
| `connectors`      | `true`  |
| `decreaseColor`   | —       |
| `increaseColor`   | —       |
| `legend`          | —       |
| `stacked`         | `true`  |
| `subtotal`        | —       |
| `totalColor`      | —       |
| `connectorConfig` | —       |
| `tooltipConfig`   | —       |

Defined in: [charts/Waterfall/index.ts:292](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/charts/Waterfall/index.ts#L292)

Creates a waterfall chart: one bar per category (`x`, or `y` with
`discrete("y")` for horizontal bars) whose value is the change it makes
to a running total. Each bar floats from where the previous bar ended;
rows marked by `subtotal` draw from zero to the running total. Bars are
colored as increases, decreases, or totals, and labeled with their change.
Each `groupBy` series keeps its own running total, drawn side by side.

The value axis includes zero by default. To zoom in on a bridge between
large totals (say 1,000 to 1,020), set a `yDomain` (`xDomain` for
horizontal bars) that stops short of zero, e.g. `yDomain([980])`: the
axis keeps zero behind a break, as BarChart does, and subtotal bars rise
from zero through it.

| <a id="property-rangebreaks"></a> `rangeBreaks?`                 | `false` \| [`RangeBreakRule`](#rangebreakrule) \| [`RangeBreakRule`](#rangebreakrule)[]               | Stretches of time to hide from a time axis, so the data closes up around them (like weekends and nights on a stock chart): one rule or a list of them. `"weekends"` hides every Saturday and Sunday; `{days: [5, 6]}` hides those days of the week (0 is Sunday); `{hours: [17, 9]}` hides the same hours every day, wrapping past midnight when the first is later (fractions are minutes, so `9.5` is 9:30); `{values: [date, …]}` hides each listed date's whole day, such as holidays; and `{bounds: [start, end]}` hides one range, from `start` up to `end`. A rule's `marker` draws the `break` marker where its time was removed, in a gap of `breakConfig.space` pixels: on by default for `bounds`, off for the others, which recur too often to mark. **Example** `{rangeBreaks: ["weekends", {hours: [16, 9.5]}, {values: ["2024-07-04"]}]}` | [utils/D3plusConfig.ts:188](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/D3plusConfig.ts#L188) |

<a id="calloutannotation"></a>

### CalloutAnnotation

Defined in: [charts/features/annotationTypes.ts:58](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/charts/features/annotationTypes.ts#L58)

A callout annotation (`{shape: "Callout", data: [...]}` in `annotations`):
a note anchored at each row's `x`/`y` (or `x2`/`y2`, on those axes), drawn
as wrapped text in a box offset from the anchor by `dx`/`dy` pixels, with
a connector line from the box to the anchor ending in an arrowhead or a
dot. Each style key takes a constant or a `(d, i)` accessor, and a row's
own key of the same name wins over a constant. The box stays inside the
plot area. Callouts draw in front of the data unless `layer: "back"`, and
never respond to the pointer or keyboard.

- [`AnnotationTextStyle`](#annotationtextstyle)

A function picks one on each render: it receives the numeric values the scale is built from (sorted, without null or NaN) and their `[min, max]` extent, with the ColorScale as `this`, and returns a scale name, as in `(values, [min, max]) => max - min > 5 ? "jenks" : "linear"`. An unknown name logs a warning and builds a linear scale. Defaults to `"linear"`, and to `"jenks"` in a chart's `colorScaleConfig`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | [utils/D3plusConfig.ts:783](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/D3plusConfig.ts#L783) |

| <a id="property-axishover"></a> `axisHover?`                                         | `boolean` \| `"x"` \| `"y"`                                                                                                                                                                           | Whether hovering a Plot's mark draws a dashed guide from its point to each axis and a badge on that axis with the point's value there, formatted as the tooltip formats that axis's values (the axis's `tickFormat` when set). `"x"` or `"y"` draws them for that direction only (each including its secondary axis). A bar is badged on its value axis only. With a discrete axis, the shared tooltip's crosshair is that axis's guide, and the value axis follows the hovered series' point (or the one nearest the pointer). Defaults to `true` (`"x"` on BumpChart, whose y axes label series rather than values, and on Streamgraph, whose y positions name no values). | <a id="property-baseline-1"></a> `baseline?`                                         | `number`                                                                                                                                                                                              | Starts a Plot's value axis (the x axis for horizontal charts) at a value: `baseline(n)` renders exactly like `yDomain([n])` (or `xDomain([n])`). Bars, areas, and stems still grow from the chart's own `0` in the Plots that draw from one (such as BarChart, AreaPlot, Histogram, and Lollipop), so with `baselineBreak` on (their default) the axis breaks back to a `0` tick and bars run through the break, with its gap cut across them, and with it off the axis stretches down to `0`. As with `yDomain([n])`, only `n` is pinned: the far end comes from the data and is rounded where the axis would round it with no domain set (left at the data when the axis config's `rounding` is "none"), and marks for values past `n` stop at the axis's edge. When every value sits at or below `n`, it ends the axis instead, like `yDomain([undefined, n])`. A bound given in `yDomain`/`xDomain` wins.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | [utils/D3plusConfig.ts:1021](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/D3plusConfig.ts#L1021) |
| <a id="property-baselinebreak-1"></a> `baselineBreak?`                               | `boolean`                                                                                                                                                                                             | When the domain of a linear value axis stops short of the `baseline` (e.g. `[1100, 2100]` with a baseline of `0`), keeps the baseline as the axis's end tick and breaks the axis between it and the domain: a short stretch of axis holds the baseline tick and two tilted marks with a gap in the axis line, then the domain spans the rest. Style it with the axis's `baselineBreakConfig`. In a Plot it applies to a user-supplied value domain (`yDomain`/`yConfig.domain`, or the x versions for horizontal charts), and bars and areas start at the baseline tick, with the break's gap cut across them (`baselineBreakConfig`'s `mask`); turned off, a `yDomain` stretches to reach the baseline while a `yConfig.domain` is kept and cuts its bars off at the axis. Defaults to `true` for the Plots whose marks grow from `0`, such as BarChart, AreaPlot, Histogram, and Lollipop (each chart lists its own default), and `false` for other Plots and a standalone Axis. | <a id="property-confidenceconfig"></a> `confidenceConfig?`                           | `Record`\<`string`, `unknown`\>                                                                                                                                                                       | Styles the `confidence` interval: a line's band (an Area) or a bar's error bar (a Path, with `stroke`, `strokeWidth`, and `capWidth` — the end caps' length in pixels or as a percentage string of the bar's thickness). Keys nested under `Area` or `Bar` apply only to that shape. `tooltip: false` leaves the bounds out of tooltips. With nested bands, `bandOpacity` sets how each band looks where it is the innermost band drawn — an array ramps from the outermost band to the innermost (default `[0.15, 0.6]`), a number gives every band that opacity — in place of `fillOpacity`. Accepted keys: any Area or Path key, `bandOpacity`, `capWidth`, `tooltip`, `Area` (Area keys), and `Bar` (Path keys and `capWidth`); any other key logs a warning. | <a id="property-connectgaps"></a> `connectGaps?`                                     | [`ConnectGaps`](#connectgaps)                                                                                                                                                                         | How a line crosses a missing value: a step of the discrete axis that another line has and this one skips, or a row whose value is `null` or `NaN`. `true` (the default) or `"solid"` draws the line straight on through it. `false` breaks the line there, leaving the gap empty. `"dashed"` breaks the line and bridges the gap with a short dash (`"2 4"`) in the line's color, distinct from a forecast's longer dash. An object styles the bridge: `stroke` (default the line's color), `strokeDasharray` (default `"2 4"`; `false` for a solid bridge), `strokeWidth` (default the line's width), and `opacity` (default `1`). A bridge follows the line's curve, since it is drawn along the same path, and is decoration only: it has no tooltip, takes no keyboard focus, and a shared tooltip at a missing step lists no value for that line. Confidence bands are clipped to the stretches between gaps. A point with a gap on both sides draws no line of its own, so turn on `lineMarkers` to show it. Areas, including stacked ones, are drawn as before. | <a id="property-contourconfig"></a> `contourConfig?`                                 | `ContourConfig`                                                                                                                                                                                       | Hexbin: contour options. `bandwidth` is the density kernel's standard deviation in pixels (default `20`); `thresholds` is about how many levels to draw (default `8`, rounded to nice values) or the levels themselves, in observations per bin; `strokeWidth` is the outline width of `"lines"` contours (default `1.5`); and `fillOpacity` is the opacity of the highest `"filled"` level (default `0.8`). `labels` (default `true`) writes each level's value along its contour lines, as a topographic map labels elevation: centered on the line, which breaks beneath it, reading upright, and clear of the other contours and labels. A long contour takes more than one label, at least `labelSpacing` pixels apart (default `"auto"`: 20 ems or half the plot's mean side, whichever is longer); `labelStep` labels every n-th level (`1` all of them, `2` every other one, keeping the multiples of twice the levels' spacing; default `"auto"`: all of up to five levels, else every other one); and a level with no clear, gently curving stretch goes unlabelled. `labelConfig` is TextBox config for the labels (`fontSize` defaults to `10`), and `levelFormat` formats their values. Merged into the current config. | <a id="property-dataformat"></a> `dataFormat?`                                       | (`data`: `DataPoint`[]) => `Record`\<`string`, `unknown`\> \| `DataPoint`[]                                                                                                                           | Transforms `data` before it is drawn. The function receives the loaded file (or the parsed JSON response, or an Array of them when `data` lists several URLs), or the Array passed as `data`, and returns the rows to draw. It may instead return a config object holding the rows as its `data` key, and the rest of that object is applied to the chart, so a response can set options such as `title` from what it contains. It runs when the chart renders, whichever order `data` and `dataFormat` are set in, and setting it again re-runs it on the next render, over the cached response (see `cache`). Every `dataPollingInterval` poll runs it too. Passing a formatter as the second argument of `data(url, format)` sets it, and setting `data` alone keeps it. [utils/D3plusConfig.ts:1359](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/D3plusConfig.ts#L1359) |
| <a id="property-datapollinginterval"></a> `dataPollingInterval?`                     | `number` \| `false`                                                                                                                                                                                   | When `data` is loaded from a URL (or a request object, or an Array holding one), re-fetches it every this many milliseconds and redraws with a transition when it changes, keeping hover, zoom, legend toggles, and the timeline selection. Each poll uses the same request and `dataFormat` as the first load, and a response identical to the drawn data is not redrawn. Polling waits while the browser tab is hidden or, with `detectVisible`, while the chart is scrolled out of view, and catches up as soon as it is visible again. A failed request keeps the last data, logs one warning per run of failures, and tries again on the next tick. `destroy()`, setting this to `false`, or passing new `data` stops polling. Only `data` is polled, not `links`, `nodes`, or `topojson`. Defaults to `false` (load once). | <a id="property-detectvisibleunload"></a> `detectVisibleUnload?`                     | `boolean`                                                                                                                                                                                             | When `true` (the default) and `detectVisible` is enabled, the Viz releases its DOM and scene while it is scrolled out of view and redraws when it returns, keeping the page light when there are many visualizations. Data and configuration are retained; interaction state such as zoom or selection is not, so set this to `false` to keep it. With `detectVisible` enabled, each chart's `<svg>` is also given `content-visibility: auto`, so the browser skips rendering its contents while it is far off-screen (this matters most when this is `false` and charts are kept). For a larger saving you can also apply `content-visibility: auto` and a `contain-intrinsic-size` to the container element yourself; that adds paint containment to an element you own, so it is not done automatically. Requires `IntersectionObserver`. | <a id="property-forecast"></a> `forecast?`                                           | `string` \| `number` \| `boolean` \| `Date` \| ((`d`: `DataPoint`, `i`: `number`) => `number` \| `boolean`)                                                                                           | Marks a forecast: the stretch of the discrete axis after it gets a shaded backdrop, a rule at its start, and a translated "Forecast" label, and each line's forecast stretch is dashed (see `forecastConfig`). A function flags the forecast rows (e.g. `d => d.Type === "Predicted"`): each line is dashed from its last unflagged point, or throughout when every row is flagged, and the backdrop starts at the earliest of those. `"auto"` (or `true`) flags the rows whose `confidence` bounds spread away from their line. A discrete-axis value (a date or year on a time axis) starts the forecast there. Unset (the default), only a trend line projection (`trendLineConfig.projection`) is marked, from the last fitted value; `false` marks nothing, not even a projection. On bar charts the backdrop starts at the edge of the first forecast bar, and bars keep their own styles. Defaults to `"auto"` on a FanChart. Bullet: each row's forecast (or other comparative measure), drawn as a paler bar behind the measure: a data key, an accessor returning the row's value, a number shared by every row, or `false`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | [utils/D3plusConfig.ts:1515](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/D3plusConfig.ts#L1515) |
| <a id="property-forecastconfig"></a> `forecastConfig?`                               | `Record`\<`string`, `unknown`\>                                                                                                                                                                       | Styles for the `forecast` marker: the backdrop's `fill` and `fillOpacity` (default `0.05`; `fill: false` hides it), the rule's `stroke`, `strokeWidth` (`1`), `strokeOpacity` (`0.4`), and `strokeDasharray` (`"4 4"`; `stroke: false` hides it), the label's text as `label` (default "Forecast", translated; `false` hides it) with `fontColor`, `fontFamily`, `fontSize` (`12`), `fontWeight`, and `fontOpacity` (`0.7`), and `lineDasharray`, the dash pattern of each line's forecast stretch (default `"6 4"`; `false` keeps lines solid). Colors default to the chart's text color for its background. The backdrop is chart chrome with no data row, so `shapeConfig.texture` and `shapeConfig.backgroundImage` leave it plain; give it its own `texture` (a textures.js name or config, drawn in the backdrop's color over its shade at `textureOpacity`, default `0.3`, with `textureDefault`) or `backgroundImage` (a URL, fit by `backgroundImageFit`, `"cover"` or `"contain"`). Both are off by default. Bullet: the forecast bar's `size` (a fraction of the band's thickness), `opacity`, `fill`, `texture`, and `backgroundImage`/`backgroundImageFit`, each a value or a `(d, i)` accessor. | <a id="property-hoverdistance"></a> `hoverDistance?`                                 | `number`                                                                                                                                                                                              | How close, in pixels, the pointer has to come to a point mark for it to count as hovering that point. Over empty space, or over something other than a point (a gridline, a link), the pointer acts on the closest point whose edge lies within this distance: its tooltip, hover highlight, and axis guides show, and a click there clicks it. A point's tooltip points at the top of the point (on it or near it) and holds still until another point takes over. Applies to the point marks of scatter and bubble plots (Circle and Rect shapes, Beeswarm included), Network nodes, and Geomap points; bars, areas, lines, and other area-filling marks keep exact hit-testing. Plots with a discrete axis and `tooltipShared` on snap to the nearest column instead. Defaults to `20`; `0` turns it off, along with the anchored tooltip. | <a id="property-keyboardnav"></a> `keyboardNav?`                                     | `boolean`                                                                                                                                                                                             | Lets keyboard users move between the chart's data marks. The chart is one Tab stop (a focusable `role="application"` element laid over it, named by `svgTitle` or the chart's `title`); once it has focus, the arrow keys move to the nearest mark in that direction, Home and End jump to the first and last mark, Enter or Space selects the focused mark as a click would (drilling down, or toggling a legend item), and Escape clears it. The focused mark shows its tooltip and hover highlight, a ring outlines it (see `keyboardNavConfig`), and a live region announces its label to screen readers. Legend items are included after the chart's marks; Line and Area series are visited point by point. On by default; `false` removes the Tab stop. | <a id="property-labelposition"></a> `labelPosition?`                                 | `"auto"` \| `"along"` \| `"inside"` \| `"outside"` \| ((`d`: `DataPoint`, `i`: `number`) => `"auto"` \| `"along"` \| `"inside"` \| `"outside"`)                                                       | Where each shape's label goes, as a string for every shape or a `(d, i) => string` accessor of the data row. - Ring segments (Donut slices and those of a Pie with an `innerRadius`, Sunburst arcs, Chord groups, and RadialBar tracks): `"along"` runs a segment's name along its arc, following the ring, reading left to right on the bottom half as on the top. `"auto"` picks, segment by segment, whichever reads better: the curve when its arc is long enough for the whole name and it shows it larger than a straight label could (a thin ring), the straight label when that fits as well, and a curve cut short with an ellipsis when nothing else fits. A full Pie (no `innerRadius`) keeps its labels inside straight: its wedges run to a point at the center. On a Pie or Donut (any `innerRadius`, and partial rings such as a half pie), a slice whose label inside can't show its whole name under `"auto"` is labelled outside the ring instead, and `"outside"` labels every slice there: its name and share, horizontal, in the Path `labelConfig`'s font at its `fontSize` (12px by default), in the theme's text color unless `labelConfig.fontColor` sets one, joined to the slice by a thin leader line. These labels stack in a column on the side of the ring their slice faces, wrapping onto a second line between words when their column is narrow; the ring shrinks (its hole with it) to leave room for them, never below 60% of its full radius, and when they don't all fit, the smallest slices' labels are left out (those slices keep their label inside, if any). `"inside"` keeps a Pie or Donut's labels straight inside their slices, and on the other ring segments both `"inside"` and `"outside"` keep the straight labels. A Donut's curves follow the middle of its ring (the rim, when its hole is small), with the slice's share on a smaller second line when there is room. A Sunburst also weighs a label turned along its radius, which suits the narrow arcs of the outer rings. Curved Donut and Sunburst names keep 5px from the ring's edges and at least 0.3em from the segment's ends, at the largest size from the Path `labelConfig`'s `fontSize` (else `fontMax`, 24px by default) down to its `fontMin` (8px). A Chord curves its group names just outside the ring when every name fits along its arc, which leaves the ring more room; otherwise it curves those that fit and turns the rest along their spokes, all at the Path `labelConfig`'s `fontSize` (11px by default). A Radar does the same with its metric names, just outside the web, each between its neighbors' spokes, wrapping a long name onto a second curved line. A RadialBar curves each track's name along the track, inside its bar (or past its end when the bar is too short), when the sweep leaves no room before the start for the straight labels, and at any sweep for `"along"`; when every track is named this way, the default legend hides. Curved text takes the color that contrasts with what lies under it (the theme's ink outside the ring) and dims with its segment on hover. A label with no room is left out. - Bars: `"inside"` or `"outside"` the bar, or `"auto"`, which goes outside when the bar is shorter than half the room along its axis. Stacked bars always label inside. - Circles (scatter and bubble points, Beeswarm points given a `label`, Network nodes, and Geomap coordinate points): `"auto"` keeps a label inside its circle when it fits there at `pointLabelConfig.fontMin` or larger, else moves it beside the circle, else hides it. A Network or Geomap's labels beside their circles stay in the chart area, a Plot's in its plot area. `"inside"` keeps every label inside, shrinking it to fit (a label that can't fit is dropped). `"outside"` always puts it beside the circle. A label goes beside its circle on the side with the most open room: the side facing its Voronoi cell's centroid first, then right, left, top, bottom, and the diagonals. A side is taken only where the label lies mostly in the circle's Voronoi cell, stays in that area, and overlaps no circle and no label placed before it. Larger circles are placed first. A label with no room is hidden; the circle's tooltip and aria-label still name it. Geomap points are labeled by `shapeConfig.Circle.label` when it is set (`false` turns their labels off), else by `label`. Labels are placed when the chart draws: a zoomed Plot places them again for its new scales, while a zoomed Network or Geomap scales them with the picture. - Stacked areas (StackedArea, Streamgraph, and a stacked AreaPlot): `"auto"` or `"along"` runs each series' name along its band's centerline, following its curve, on the stretch where the band is at least the font size plus 4px thick under the whole label and flattest. The text reads upright, in the color that contrasts with the band's fill (or the Area `labelConfig`'s `fontColor`, when you set one), and dims with its band on hover. It starts at the Area `labelConfig`'s `fontSize` (or `fontMax`, else 16px) and shrinks a pixel at a time down to its `fontMin`, but no lower than 8px, before giving up; a band too thin for its name everywhere goes unlabeled. When every band gets a name, the default legend hides (a `legend` of your own always wins, and the legend stays while a series is hidden from it). `"inside"` (or `"outside"`) puts the label in the band's largest box instead. `shapeConfig.Area.label` sets the text, or `false` for none. Defaults to `"auto"`. | [utils/D3plusConfig.ts:1773](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/D3plusConfig.ts#L1773) |

The column fits the widest label up to it, wrapping or truncating longer ones; `0` hides it. | <a id="property-legendhistory"></a> `legendHistory?`                                 | `boolean`                                                                                                                                                                                             | Whether legend clicks go on the chart's Back history. A click or shift+click (or Enter or Space on a legend item) that changes what is hidden or solo'd shows the Back button, and Back undoes legend clicks and drill-downs in the order they happened, restoring the legend exactly as it was. A drill-down to a deeper level starts with every group shown, and Back out of it brings back the legend it left. A click that changes nothing adds no step, and new `data` clears the legend's steps along with the legend. Clicking a Sunburst or Icicle center zooms out without undoing the legend clicks made since the zoom. Defaults to `true`; `false` leaves legend clicks off the history, so Back only steps out of drill-downs. | <a id="property-legendinset"></a> `legendInset?`                                     | `boolean` \| ((`config`: [`D3plusConfig`](#d3plusconfig)) => `boolean`)                                                                                                                               | Whether the chart may draw one of its legends inside the empty space around its marks instead of in a margin, for charts that leave open space around their marks, such as Plot and the charts built on it, Network, Pack, Pie, and Geomap; a chart whose marks fill its area, like Treemap, keeps its legends in the margins. After the chart lays out, the size legend is tried first, then the legend, then the colorScale; the first that fits is drawn over a semi-transparent box (see `legendInsetConfig`), and any others keep their margins. Space enclosed by the marks, like the middle of a ring of points, is never used. Only a legend or colorScale whose position is `"auto"` (the default) can move inside; one set to a side stays in that margin. Defaults to `true`; also accepts a function that receives the resolved chart config and returns a boolean. | <a id="property-linelabelconfig"></a> `lineLabelConfig?`                             | `LineLabelConfig`                                                                                                                                                                                     | Options for `lineLabels`. `value: true` adds the line's value at each labeled end after the series name (e.g. "Brazil 37%"), formatted as the y axis formats its ticks (its `tickFormat` when set). `valueFormat` formats it instead, as a function of the value, the row it belongs to, and the row's index. Defaults to `{value: false}`.                                                                                      | [utils/D3plusConfig.ts:1909](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/D3plusConfig.ts#L1909) |
| <a id="property-linelabels"></a> `lineLabels?`                                       | `LineLabelsSetting`                                                                                                                                                                                   | Labels each line of a line chart with its series name, just past the line's ends: `true` or `"end"` labels the right end, `"start"` the left end, and `"both"` both ends. A function of each row returns any of these (or `false`) to choose per series. The plot leaves room for the labels on the side they sit, at most a quarter of its width past the y axis per side; a label wider than that drops its value, then shortens its name with an ellipsis, then hides. Labels that would overlap are moved apart, each side on its own, with a dotted connector back to their line; when the plot is too short for them all, the last that fits reads "+N more". `lineLabelConfig` adds each end's value to its label. `"along"` writes each series name along its own line instead, following its curve: on the stretch that bends and slopes least and stays clear of the other lines and labels, reading upright whichever way the line runs. A line with no clear stretch for its name goes unlabeled, a chart (or small-multiples panel) with a single line names none, and the plot leaves no room past the lines for these labels. The Line shape's `labelConfig` sets their `fontSize`, `fontFamily`, and `fontWeight`. When every line gets a name, the default legend hides (a `legend` of your own always wins). LinePlot defaults to `"along"`; other charts default to no labels. | <a id="property-link"></a> `link?`                                                   | [`LinkOption`](#linkoption)                                                                                                                                                                           | Links this chart to every other chart with the same group name, so hovering, `active`, `highlight` (including search), and legend hide/solo clicks in one are mirrored in the rest, and a value gets the same categorical color in every chart. Rows match across charts by the value of `by` (a data key or accessor), which defaults to the chart's own id. A string is shorthand for `{group}`; set `hover`, `active`, `highlight`, `legend`, or `color` to `false` to stop sharing that behavior. | <a id="property-linkbundle"></a> `linkBundle?`                                       | `boolean`                                                                                                                                                                                             | Network and Geomap: bundles the links (force-directed edge bundling, after Holten and van Wijk). Links that run the same way near each other are pulled together into shared curves that fan out at their ends, so the main flows read through the clutter of a dense chart. Arrowheads, labels, hover, and click focus follow each bundled curve. A Network's links from a node to itself, and a Geomap's links on a globe or cut by its projection, are drawn as usual; a bundled Geomap link ignores `linkCurve`. The bundling is worked out once per layout (under a second for 2,500 links) and reused while the chart zooms, pans, or is hovered. Defaults to `false`. | <a id="property-linkbundleconfig"></a> `linkBundleConfig?`                           | `LinkBundleConfig`                                                                                                                                                                                    | Tunes `linkBundle`: `strength` (how closely links keep to their bundles, `0.85`), `cycles` (`6`), `iterations` (`50`), `compatibility` (how alike two links must be to bundle, `0.4`; lower bundles more), and `smoothing` (`true` draws smooth curves). Merged into the defaults. | <a id="property-linkcolor"></a> `linkColor?`                                         | `string` \| `false` \| ((`d`: `DataPoint`, `i`: `number`) => `unknown`)                                                                                                                               | Colors each link of a Network, Rings, Sankey, ArcDiagram, or Geomap, and its arrowheads: `"source"` or `"target"` takes that end node's color, and a key or accessor function reads a value from each link (receiving the link, with `source` and `target` set to the data of its nodes, and its index in `links`). A number is colored on the chart's colorScale, which then shows the links' values beside the nodes' color legend (when the chart also has a `colorScale` for its nodes, nodes and links share it, on one domain); a string is a color when it parses as one, or else a category in the chart's palette, as `color` colors nodes. `false` (the default) draws every link in the theme's `link` gray (on a Geomap, a gray halfway between the chart's background and text colors, which reads over land and water alike). | <a id="property-linkcurve"></a> `linkCurve?`                                         | `number`                                                                                                                                                                                              | Geomap: how far each link bows into an arc, as a share of the distance between its ends. `0` draws the plain great-circle path; the default `0.2` lifts a link's middle by a fifth of that distance, to the left of its direction (a negative value bows to the right), so links running both ways between two places stay apart. On a flat map, a link whose great circle the projection cuts (across the antimeridian, or between `"geoAlbersUsa"`'s insets) is drawn on the screen between its ends, bowed the same way, so it crosses the map instead of leaving by one edge. On a projection that clips to a circle (a globe such as `"geoOrthographic"`), links follow the great circle without the lift. | <a id="property-linklabel"></a> `linkLabel?`                                         | `string` \| ((`d`: `DataPoint`, `i`: `number`) => `unknown`)                                                                                                                                          | Text drawn at the middle of each link of a Network, Rings, Sankey, ArcDiagram, or Geomap: a key or accessor function (receiving the link, with `source` and `target` set to the data of its nodes, and its index in `links`). It sits halfway along a link's length, centered on a Sankey band, and at the top of an ArcDiagram arc, on a pad of the chart's background, and follows a curved link's curve (see `linkLabelConfig`). Numbers are abbreviated in the chart's locale. Labels that would cover a node or another label are hidden, the widest links' labels kept first. Defaults to none. | <a id="property-linklabelconfig"></a> `linkLabelConfig?`                             | `LinkLabelConfig`                                                                                                                                                                                     | Styles the link labels (see `linkLabel`): `rotate`, `"along"` (the default) to run text along its link, kept upright, or `"horizontal"`; `fontSize` (10); `padding`, the pad around the text (2); `backgroundOpacity`, the opacity of that pad in the chart's background color (0.85); `minRadius`, the tightest bend a curved label follows, in ems (2); and any other TextBox setting, such as `fontColor` (defaults to the chart's text color), `fontFamily`, or `fontWeight`. Along a curved link (a Rings spline or fanned parallel link, an ArcDiagram arc, a self-loop, a bundled Network edge, a Geomap flow arc, or a Sankey band or return lane), an `"along"` label follows the curve, centered where a straight label would sit, over a pad that curves with it, and is cut short with an ellipsis when the curve has too little room (or left out when fewer than three letters fit). A loop bending tighter than `minRadius` keeps a straight label. | <a id="property-outerpadding"></a> `outerPadding?`                                   | `number` \| `"auto"`                                                                                                                                                                                  | Room (px) the Radar reserves around its web for the metric labels. `"auto"` (the default) curves every metric name along the web when they all fit (see `labelPosition`), on one line or, for long names, two, which needs only that much room. Otherwise it measures the labels along their spokes and gives the web the largest radius at which every label fits inside the chart, wrapping long labels onto two lines (and truncating what still doesn't fit) rather than shrinking the web below half its largest possible size; names that fit along the web at that radius still curve. A number reserves exactly that much room and wraps labels to that width. | <a id="property-reducedmotion"></a> `reducedMotion?`                                 | `boolean` \| `"auto"`                                                                                                                                                                                 | Whether the chart animates. `"auto"` (default) follows the viewer's OS setting, read from the `(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` media query at each draw (server-side rendering counts as not reduced). `true` always draws without motion: shapes, axes, legends, zooms, and fades jump straight to their final state. `false` always animates. `duration` keeps the value you set either way. [utils/D3plusConfig.ts:2247](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/D3plusConfig.ts#L2247) |
| <a id="property-referencebands"></a> `referenceBands?`                               | [`ReferenceBandConfig`](#referencebandconfig)[]                                                                                                                                                       | Plot: shaded spans across the plot between two values, such as a recession or a target range. Give each entry `x` (a vertical band) or `y` (a horizontal one) as `[start, end]` in data units (numbers, dates, or categories; on a category axis the band covers each end category's whole slot), or `x2`/`y2` for the secondary axes, or `ref: "plot"` for fractions of the plot area. An optional `label` sits inside the band's top-left corner (`labelPosition: "end"` for the top-right), with `fontColor`, `fontFamily`, `fontSize`, `fontWeight`, `lineHeight`, and `maxWidth`. The fill defaults to the chart's text color at `fillOpacity` `0.08`, so it reads on light and dark themes; `stroke`, `strokeWidth`, and `strokeOpacity` add edges. On a continuous or time axis the band's ends count toward the axis domain, widening it to show the whole band (an end set by `xDomain`/`yDomain`/`x2Domain`/`y2Domain` or the axis config's `domain` stays put). Each entry expands into a `"ReferenceBand"` annotation (see `annotations`) behind the data (`layer: "front"` to draw it over; its label always draws above), which follows zoom and never responds to the pointer or keyboard. A label that would cover a data label or another reference label moves to the band's other corners or along its length, inside the plot, and is hidden when no spot is free.
