                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | [utils/D3plusConfig.ts:2269](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/D3plusConfig.ts#L2269) |
| <a id="property-referencelines"></a> `referenceLines?`                               | [`ReferenceLineConfig`](#referencelineconfig)[]                                                                                                                                                       | Plot: lines across the whole plot at one value, such as a target or a launch date. Give each entry `x` (a vertical line) or `y` (a horizontal one) in data units (a number, a date, or a category), or `x2`/`y2` for the secondary axes, or `ref: "plot"` for a fraction of the plot area. An optional `label` sits at the line's `"end"` (the right of a horizontal line, the top of a vertical one) or `"start"` (`labelPosition`), with `fontColor`, `fontFamily`, `fontSize`, `fontWeight`, `lineHeight`, and `maxWidth`. The line's `stroke` defaults to the chart's text color at `strokeOpacity` `0.6`, `strokeWidth` `1`; `dash: true` dashes it ("4 4"), or give a dash pattern. On a continuous or time axis the value counts toward the axis domain, widening it to show the line (an end set by `xDomain`/`yDomain`/ `x2Domain`/`y2Domain` or the axis config's `domain` stays put; a value outside such a domain is not drawn). Each entry expands into a `"ReferenceLine"` annotation (see `annotations`) behind the data (`layer: "front"` to draw it over; its label always draws above), which follows zoom and never responds to the pointer or keyboard. A label that would cover a data label or another reference label moves to the line's other side or end, or along it, inside the plot, and is hidden when no spot is free. | <a id="property-sizezero"></a> `sizeZero?`                                           | `boolean`                                                                                                                                                                                             | Anchors a Plot's size scale at zero, so a mark's size is proportional to its value: with the default `sizeScale` of `"sqrt"`, each circle's area is (a value twice as large draws a circle with twice the area), and with `"linear"`, its radius. | <a id="property-swarm"></a> `swarm?`                                                 | `boolean` \| `"x"` \| `"y"` \| `"auto"`                                                                                                                                                               | Packs a Plot's circles into a beeswarm: each circle keeps its value along one axis and is placed beside its neighbors along the other, so none overlap. `"x"` or `"y"` names the value axis; `true` uses x when its values are numeric, else y; `false` draws a plain scatter. When the other axis holds categories (strings), each category gets its own swarm in its own band; otherwise that axis's values are ignored and its axis is hidden. Circles keep their ids, so switching a chart between `false` and `true` animates each circle between its scatter and swarm position. The default, `"auto"`, swarms only when every mark is a Circle and every row lacks a y (or x) value.                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | [utils/D3plusConfig.ts:2493](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/D3plusConfig.ts#L2493) |
| <a id="property-swarmconfig"></a> `swarmConfig?`                                     | `object`                                                                                                                                                                                              | Options for `swarm`: `padding`, the minimum pixel gap between circles (default `1`), and `overflow`, what happens when a swarm is wider than its band — `"shrink"` (default) scales every circle down until each swarm fits, `"clamp"` keeps the sizes and holds outlying circles at the band's edge, and `"visible"` lets swarms spill past their band. | <a id="property-theme"></a> `theme?`                                                 | [`ThemeSetting`](#themesetting)                                                                                                                                                                       | The chart's colors. `"auto"` (the default) paints no background and follows the page behind the chart: its chrome text contrasts with the page, its tooltip, table view, and overlays turn dark on a dark page, and it redraws when the page flips between light and dark. `"light"` and `"dark"` paint the theme's background behind the chart (so it reads the same on any page, and in a saved image) and take every chrome color from the theme. An object sets your own tokens on top of the preset its `base` names (`"light"` or `"dark"`), for example `{base: "dark", background: "#123", accent: "#ffd43b"}`. A dark theme also turns color scale ramps around, from a dim tint near the background up to a bright pole (see the `colorScale` tokens). Colors you set in the other config (`titleConfig.fontColor`, `tooltipConfig`, `colorScaleConfig.colorMax`, the `*Style` options, …) win over the theme.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | [utils/D3plusConfig.ts:2578](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/D3plusConfig.ts#L2578) |
| <a id="property-threshold"></a> `threshold?`                                         | `number`                                                                                                                                                                                              | Threshold value for grouping small slices, as a share of the total (`0.05` is 5%). On a stacked Plot (StackedArea, or an AreaPlot, BarChart, or LinePlot with `stacked`), the series whose summed value across every position is under that share of the whole chart's total merge into one series, labelled by `thresholdName` and stacked on top. A bucket needs at least two items (a lone small item stays as itself), and its tooltips list the items it holds with their values. Off by default on Plot charts. | <a id="property-xdomain"></a> `xDomain?`                                             | (`string` \| `number` \| `Date`)[]                                                                                                                                                                    | The x domain as an array. On a continuous axis it is `[min, max]`. Setting just one end (`[min]` or `[undefined, max]`) pins only that end: the data fills the other, rounded where the axis would round it with no domain set (left at the data when `xConfig`'s `rounding` is "none"; time axes aren't rounded). With both ends set, neither is rounded. On a discrete axis it lists the categories to show, in order; data in other categories is not drawn. A full `xConfig` `domain` is the lower-level override: it wins over this, and is drawn exactly as given (rounded only by `xConfig`'s own `rounding`), without stretching to the chart's `baseline`. | <a id="property-zoomcontrolicons"></a> `zoomControlIcons?`                           | `Partial`\<`Record`\<`"zoomIn"` \| `"zoomOut"` \| `"zoomReset"` \| `"zoomBrush"`, `string` \| ((`el`: `HTMLElement`) => `void` \| (() => `void`))\>\>                                                 | Overrides one or more of the four built-in zoom-control icons (`zoomIn`, `zoomOut`, `zoomReset`, `zoomBrush`), which otherwise render as inline SVGs. Each value is either an HTML string — used as the button's content in place of the built-in icon — or a mount function, `(el: HTMLElement) => void \| (() => void)`, called once with the button's reserved icon slot (a 12x12px element) so you can mount anything imperative into it: a React tree (`createRoot(el).render(<Icon/>)`), a Vue app, a canvas sprite, a brand `<img>`. Return a cleanup function from the mount function if there's teardown to do; it runs right before that slot is discarded — which happens whenever the whole button panel's markup regenerates (a `.locale(...)` change, a `zoomControlClassName` change, or the brush toggle switching), not just once per chart. <a id="referencebandconfig"></a>

### ReferenceBandConfig

Defined in: [charts/features/annotationTypes.ts:150](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/charts/features/annotationTypes.ts#L150)

A shaded span across the plot between two values: give `x` (a vertical
band) or `y` (a horizontal one) as `[start, end]`, or `x2`/`y2`. On a
category axis the band covers each end category's whole slot; on a
continuous or time axis its ends widen the axis domain, unless the user
set that end of the domain.

### ReferenceLineConfig

Defined in: [charts/features/annotationTypes.ts:124](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/charts/features/annotationTypes.ts#L124)

A full-width or full-height line across the plot at one value: give `x`
(a vertical line) or `y` (a horizontal one), or `x2`/`y2` for the
secondary axes. On a continuous or time axis the value widens the axis
domain to show the line, unless the user set that end of the domain.

<a id="themecolorscaletokens"></a>

### ThemeColorScaleTokens

Defined in: [utils/theme.ts:56](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/theme.ts#L56)

The colors a chart's color scale (`colorScale`) and ordinal ramps
(`colorOrdinal`) take when `colorScaleConfig` doesn't set them. On a dark
theme every ramp runs from a dim tint near the background up to its bright
pole, so low values recede and high values stand out.

#### Properties

| Property                                 | Type     | Description                                                                                                                                               | Defined in                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| <a id="property-max-1"></a> `max`        | `string` | The high end of single-hue ramps and the positive pole of diverging scales (`colorMax`).                                                                  | [utils/theme.ts:58](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/theme.ts#L58) |
| <a id="property-mid"></a> `mid`          | `string` | The midpoint of diverging scales (`colorMid`).                                                                                                            | [utils/theme.ts:60](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/theme.ts#L60) |
| <a id="property-min-1"></a> `min`        | `string` | The negative pole of diverging scales, and the hue of all-negative ramps (`colorMin`).                                                                    | [utils/theme.ts:62](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/theme.ts#L62) |
| <a id="property-missing"></a> `missing?` | `string` | The fill of marks without a value: Geomap regions and Calendar days. Unset in both presets, where each chart derives a quiet neutral from the background. | [utils/theme.ts:68](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/theme.ts#L68) |

"pointer" : "crosshair")}`                                                                                                                                                  | [utils/D3plusConfig.ts:493](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/D3plusConfig.ts#L493) |

| <a id="property-brushmax"></a> `brushMax?`                     | `number`                                                                                | The maximum number of ticks (or buttons) a selection can span; unlimited by default. Helpful for x/y plots where selecting fewer than 2 time periods is undesirable. A narrower brush widens to it on release: a drag keeps the end being dragged (or, with ticks, its first tick), and a click selects the clicked period and the ones after it. A narrower starting selection keeps its latest period, and a chart that starts on its latest period starts on its latest `brushMin` instead. Either way, the selection grows the other way where the timeline runs out. Unused with `brushing: false`. | [utils/D3plusConfig.ts:520](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/utils/D3plusConfig.ts#L520) |

<a id="rangebreakrule"></a>

### RangeBreakRule

> **RangeBreakRule** = `"weekends"` \| \{ `days`: `number`[]; `marker?`: `boolean`; \} \| \{ `hours`: \[`number`, `number`\]; `marker?`: `boolean`; \} \| \{ `marker?`: `boolean`; `values`: [`RangeBreakTime`](#rangebreaktime)[]; \} \| \{ `bounds`: \[[`RangeBreakTime`](#rangebreaktime), [`RangeBreakTime`](#rangebreaktime)\]; `marker?`: `boolean`; \}

Defined in: [components/Axis/rangeBreaks.ts:29](https://github.com/d3plus/d3plus/blob/main/packages/core/src/components/Axis/rangeBreaks.ts#L29)

One stretch of time a time axis hides:

- `"weekends"`: every Saturday and Sunday.
- `{days: [6, 0]}`: every day of the week listed (0 is Sunday, 6 is Saturday).
- `{hours: [17, 9]}`: the same hours of every day, from the first hour to
  the second (fractions are minutes, so `9.5` is 9:30); a start after the
  end wraps past midnight, so `[17, 9]` hides 5pm to 9am.
- `{values: [date, …]}`: each listed date's whole day, such as holidays.
- `{bounds: [start, end]}`: one explicit range, from `start` up to `end`.

An object rule's `marker` draws the axis's break marker where its time
was removed, leaving a short gap there. It defaults to `true` for
`bounds` and `false` for the others, which recur too often to mark.

---
